a34.speaker: Vito Tanzi, former director of the IMF's Fiscal Affairs Department
a34.name: Vito Tanzi
a34.title: former director of the IMF's Fiscal Affairs Department
a34.speech: Warned that states that grow in functions and structures become "obese," absorbing resources that should be at the service of society.

a34.speaker: Amartya Sen
a34.name: Amartya Sen
a34.speech: Pointed out that in small island countries, budgetary choices are, more than technical matters, choices of social justice: every escudo spent on privileges is an escudo taken away from a family's basic dignity.

a34.speaker: A Nação (issue No. 931, August 3, 2025)
a34.name: A Nação (issue No. 931
a34.title: August 3, 2025)
a34.speech: Reported that the personnel costs for the structure created to prepare the new Millennium Challenge Account investment program represented, at the time, a significant burden on public coffers — around 40 million escudos.

a36.speaker: Moleti Obakeng, shebeen owner and community volunteer (Motokwe, Botswana)
a36.name: Moleti Obakeng
a36.title: shebeen owner and community volunteer (Motokwe, Botswana)
a36.speech: Said that in November 2023, she was told by Red Cross volunteers that they were looking for mothers and guardians who did not take their children for child welfare care (CWC) and immunisation.

a208.speaker: Bachir Ismaël Ouédraogo, Minister of Energy of Burkina Faso
a208.name: Bachir Ismaël Ouédraogo
a208.title: Minister of Energy of Burkina Faso
a208.speech: Said these agreements constitute a step forward towards universal access to energy: "Indeed, thanks to the Yeleen programme, 52 MW more will be injected into the electricity grid with the construction of 4 photovoltaic power plants, notably 42 MW in Ouagadougou with a storage capacity of 10 MWh and other towns such as Dori and Gaoua" ; Said Yeleen will ultimately make it possible to reduce the cost of the kWh, and thanked the AFD as well as the programme's other technical and financial partners, namely the European Union and the African Development Bank.

a208.speaker: Luc Hallade, Ambassador of France to Burkina Faso
a208.name: Luc Hallade
a208.title: Ambassador of France to Burkina Faso
a208.speech: Said that beyond their significant amount, the various agreements attest to the will of the friendship between France and Burkina: "Burkina is going through difficult times and, as a friend, France wishes to support it militarily but also to help with the implementation of its public development policies."

a218.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a218.name: Donald Trump
a218.title: President of the United States
a218.speech: Claims this is a mechanism to evaluate whether USAID programmes align with his "America First" policy.

a218.speaker: Research (unnamed studies)
a218.name: Research (unnamed studies)
a218.speech: Shows that the effectiveness of aid depends on the type of support provided, how well it aligns with local needs, and the mechanisms used to deliver it.

a218.speaker: Maj. Gen. (Rtd) J. B Tjivikua, criminal intelligence analyst (opinion author)
a218.name: Maj. Gen. (Rtd) J. B Tjivikua
a218.title: criminal intelligence analyst (opinion author)
a218.speech: Argues that foreign aid by most affluent and powerful countries is rarely charity and usually comes with strings attached, a clear weaponisation of aid; that government-led foreign aid is a primary method of expanding soft power and can also be used as a method of hard power and effective foreign interference in sovereign decision-making; that foreign aid dependency generally fosters underdevelopment; and that leaders of developing nations must lead their own development to generate resources to reduce the risk of total dependence and "cease the insincere display of grief" following Trump's move to cut funding to all USAID foreign assistance programmes.

a262.speaker: Rev. Benjamin Ackah, Minister in charge of the Okye Ekyir Aldersgate Society
a262.name: Rev. Benjamin Ackah
a262.title: Minister in charge of the Okye Ekyir Aldersgate Society
a262.speech: Advised the youth in the country to eschew drug addiction, sexual immorality and the pursuit of quick riches; urged them to make God the foundation of every endeavour in order to achieve greater heights: “Horses and chariots are prepared for battle but victory comes from the Lord”, urging the youth to trust God for their upliftment ; said cutting corners for quick riches, ignoring the values of honesty and hard work, eventually had devastating consequences on individuals and families and society; said while money and wealth are important in life, their significance has been overly emphasised at the expense of values such as honesty, hard work and goodwill, and advised the youth to lawfully seek wealth, not ignoring Christian values ; described the members of the Aldersgate Society as unique people committed to the development of the church and was hopeful that the next 10 years would see the church raising well-grounded Christians committed to spreading the gospel of Jesus Christ.

a262.speaker: Very Rev. Isaac Aidoo, Superintendent Minister of the Mankessim Circuit of the Methodist Church
a262.name: Very Rev. Isaac Aidoo
a262.title: Superintendent Minister of the Mankessim Circuit of the Methodist Church
a262.speech: Urged the Aldersgate Society to work harder to spread the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ which had the power to save; commended the minister and congregation for their steadfastness which had led to the steady growth of the church.

a262.speaker: M. K. Ato Brown, Cape Coast Diocese Chairman of Methodist Choirs and a founder member of the society
a262.name: M. K. Ato Brown
a262.title: Cape Coast Diocese Chairman of Methodist Choirs and a founder member of the society
a262.speech: Acknowledged the contribution of the church to the development of members in the area, saying many youths had been supported to remain in school; paid tribute to the then Very Rev. John Buah Kwofi, Very Rev. Michael Panford, Very Rev. Emmanuel Adjei and Very Rev. John Otoo, who all contributed to the start and development of the society; called for support towards the completion of the society’s church building; advised the youth to be humble and learn to prepare themselves for the future and urged parents to train children in the fear of the Lord, saying the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

a270.speaker: Godknows Maseko, co-founder of Step Kids Awareness Trust (STEKA)
a270.name: Godknows Maseko
a270.title: co-founder of Step Kids Awareness Trust (STEKA)
a270.speech: said it was timely donation that will help the home pay fees for some of its children and develop their future ; "I am failing to thank you well enough for this gesture because it has taken me by complete surprise," he said. "We were in dilemma as to where we might get the funds to pay for school fees for some of the children in primary and secondary schools."

a270.speaker: Godknows Maseko, co-founder of Step Kids Awareness Trust (STEKA)
a270.name: Godknows Maseko
a270.title: co-founder of Step Kids Awareness Trust (STEKA)
a270.speech: disclosed that they are currently raising and educating 120 children, most of whom plucked away from street begging - of which 26 are in universities and the rest in secondary and primary schools; he also announced a success story that two of the STEKA Home products will soon be graduating as nurses and three more are expected to graduate next year.

a270.speaker: Godknows Maseko, co-founder of Step Kids Awareness Trust (STEKA)
a270.name: Godknows Maseko
a270.title: co-founder of Step Kids Awareness Trust (STEKA)
a270.speech: said just because they are situated in Nyambadwe, potential well wishers think they are well off, thus they are not supported as much as they wished they could be ; "We deliberately considered Nyambadwe as a location to operate from because we wanted to give the children a decent home so that they should not feel being alienated from the rest of other children. CDH Investment Bank ladies probably had several other vulnerable child care institutions they could have chosen to reach out to but they opted for STEKA and we profoundly thank them for their gesture. We ask other well wishers to support our children of whom 90% were taken away from the streets. Without the support from well wishers like CDH Investment Bank, we shall fail and that would mean our kids going back to the streets."

a270.speaker: Godknows Maseko, co-founder of Step Kids Awareness Trust (STEKA)
a270.name: Godknows Maseko
a270.title: co-founder of Step Kids Awareness Trust (STEKA)
a270.speech: told the CDHIB ladies that he himself was a street connected child but was plucked away from it by well wishers and he decided to share the kindness by establishing the vulnerable child care institution.

a270.speaker: Loveness Sitima, CDH Investment Bank Risk & Compliance Assistant Manager
a270.name: Loveness Sitima
a270.title: CDH Investment Bank Risk & Compliance Assistant Manager
a270.speech: said the gesture is part of helping the community to grow which the bank strongly believes and they needed to emulate; added that it was satisfying that STEKA was their right choice having been appraised of the strides the institution has made over the years which has seen many of its children being raised into responsible citizens; acknowledged that the role STEKA is playing is human capital development as enshrined in the MW2063 national vision and they are proud to have played a part in assisting the home meet some of the challenges it is facing in its obligations ; "Together we can build a better Malawi," she said. "I must say we are very overwhelmed to see the happy faces of these children, who are being raised in such a beautiful home set-up."

a270.speaker: Bertha Kapalanga, founder of Mama Berna Foundation
a270.name: Bertha Kapalanga
a270.title: founder of Mama Berna Foundation
a270.speech: said CDHIB's is the largest investment that they have received.

a270.speaker: Mercy Sekani, CDH Investment Bank Capital City Branch Manager
a270.name: Mercy Sekani
a270.title: CDH Investment Bank Capital City Branch Manager
a270.speech: said Mother's Day should not only be about celebrating mothers but also remembering children who do not have parents and she urged other well-wishers to reach out to people who are in need.

a270.speaker: The Masekos, STEKA founders
a270.name: The Masekos
a270.title: STEKA founders
a270.speech: emphasise that STEKA is not an 'orphanage' nor an 'institution' but a loving family, saying the children are brought by social services or the police and once they indicate their intention to staying for good, they make sure that all their new children who don't know their biological parents adopt their surname of Maseko.

a277.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a277.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a277.speech: says it regrets the decision of the American president and hopes that he will go back on his decree signed on 20 January, only a few hours after his inauguration; the organisation even says it is ready to engage in "constructive" dialogue with the Trump Administration in order to maintain this partnership, for the benefit of the health and well-being of millions of people around the world.

a277.speaker: Donald Trump, 47th President of the United States
a277.name: Donald Trump
a277.title: 47th President of the United States
a277.speech: accused the WHO of "fraud" on the question of vaccines against the Covid-19 pandemic; he had already tried in 2020 to withdraw his country from the organisation, which he accused at the time of being controlled by China.

a331.speaker: David Bikhado Ofungi, founder and chief executive officer of DERO and curator of the Mkutano
a331.name: David Bikhado Ofungi
a331.title: founder and chief executive officer of DERO and curator of the Mkutano
a331.speech: Said optimal funding to local governments is key for the growth of local economies that feed into the national economy ; said the ability to collect taxes, levy fees and penalties by local governments would determine their success in providing services to their people.

a331.speaker: David Bikhado Ofungi, founder and chief executive officer of DERO and curator of the Mkutano
a331.name: David Bikhado Ofungi
a331.title: founder and chief executive officer of DERO and curator of the Mkutano
a331.speech: Said the challenge is that most cities including the newly created ones have ambitious plans amidst having fastest growing populations, and that these local governments cannot raise money and fully fund their activities; he suggests the need to further embrace public private partnerships and the search for capital within the capital markets.

a331.speaker: David Bikhado Ofungi, founder and chief executive officer of DERO and curator of the Mkutano
a331.name: David Bikhado Ofungi
a331.title: founder and chief executive officer of DERO and curator of the Mkutano
a331.speech: Said there is need to amend the local government act to relax the restriction of how much local governments can borrow; currently they can only borrow 25% of their total annual revenue.

a331.speaker: Rosa Malango, UN Resident Coordinator for Uganda
a331.name: Rosa Malango
a331.title: UN Resident Coordinator for Uganda
a331.speech: Said this year’s Mkutano is quite relevant because sub-national/local governments and cities are concerned about the burgeoning infrastructure needs and the need to implement the SDGs at the local level ; said the theme is in line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework for Uganda 2020-2025 and with SDG 17.

a331.speaker: Rosa Malango, UN Resident Coordinator for Uganda
a331.name: Rosa Malango
a331.title: UN Resident Coordinator for Uganda
a331.speech: Said there is a global consensus that countries need to accelerate the implementation of SDGs, with only 10 of the 15 years remaining. “While the progress towards SDGs may vary from one goal to another, Uganda has nonetheless made significant progress towards the achievement of SDGs and has been ranked 18th among 52 African countries” ; said progress has been registered in health, gender equality, decent work and economic growth, industry innovation and infrastructure and partnerships.

a331.speaker: Rosa Malango, UN Resident Coordinator for Uganda
a331.name: Rosa Malango
a331.title: UN Resident Coordinator for Uganda
a331.speech: Said the public and private finance will both be needed - at scale - to meet the SDGs, and that official development assistance can and should play a role in catalyzing and accelerating those flows, especially in risky and harder to reach local economies ; said there is need to improve on efficiency of collection and management of existing revenues, development of innovative alternative financing options, working towards improved legal and policy regime for local governments to tap into innovative financing options and improving on credit worthiness. “We will continue to work with Government of Uganda and the Local Governments in not only these areas but bring on board innovative financing instruments.”

a331.speaker: Pamela Mbabazi, chairperson of the board of directors for the National Planning Authority
a331.name: Pamela Mbabazi
a331.title: chairperson of the board of directors for the National Planning Authority
a331.speech: Said the major problem confronting local authorities in Uganda is the widening gap between the availability of financial resources and local spending needs ; said the rapid growth of the population is creating an ever-increasing demand for public services, new public infrastructure, and its maintenance as well as other social needs ; said that during the implementation of NDPI and II, there was dwindling local revenues which are insufficient to finance local economic development and public services in local governments.

a358.speaker: UNICEF (U.N. children's agency)
a358.name: UNICEF (U.N. children's agency)
a358.speech: Said on Tuesday that funding cuts are driving an entire generation of children in Sudan to the brink of irreversible harm as support is scaled back and malnutrition cases persist across the country; said children were being cut off from life-saving services due to funding cuts while the scale of need is staggering, and that access to areas in need continues to be a challenge, with some roads rendered inaccessible due to the rainy season, hampering aid delivery.

a358.speaker: Sheldon Yett, UNICEF Representative in Sudan
a358.name: Sheldon Yett
a358.title: UNICEF Representative in Sudan
a358.speech: Speaking via video link from Port Sudan: "Children have limited access to safe water, food, healthcare. Malnutrition is rife, and many good children are reduced to just skin, bones." ; "With recent funding cuts, many of our partners in Khartoum and elsewhere have been forced to scale back… We are being stretched to the limit across Sudan, with children dying of hunger." ; "We on the verge of irreversible damage being done to an entire generation of children in Sudan."

a358.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a358.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a358.speech: Said in July that several areas to the south of Sudan's capital Khartoum are at risk of famine.

a358.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a358.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a358.speech: According to OCHA, only 23% of the 4.16 billion dollar global humanitarian response plan for Sudan has been funded.

a358.speaker: Jens Laerke, OCHA
a358.name: Jens Laerke
a358.title: OCHA
a358.speech: "It has been one year since famine was confirmed in ZamZam camp and no food has reached this area. Al-Fashir remains under siege. We need that access now."

a435.speaker: Ulf Kristersson, Swedish Prime Minister (post on X)
a435.name: Ulf Kristersson
a435.title: Swedish Prime Minister (post on X)
a435.speech: "The situation in Gaza is absolutely terrible and Israel is not respecting its most fundamental obligations nor the agreements signed on emergency humanitarian aid." ; "Therefore, Sweden demands that the European Union suspend the trade part of the association agreement as soon as possible. Economic pressure on Israel must be intensified. The Israeli Government must allow humanitarian aid to enter Gaza unhindered."

a435.speaker: Ulf Kristersson, Swedish Prime Minister (post on X)
a435.name: Ulf Kristersson
a435.title: Swedish Prime Minister (post on X)
a435.speech: "At the same time, pressure on Hamas must increase so that the hostages are released immediately and unconditionally. Sweden welcomes the fact that more countries in the Middle East are demanding that Hamas be disarmed and have no further place in a future government in Gaza."

a435.speaker: Caspar Veldkamp, Dutch Minister of Foreign Affairs
a435.name: Caspar Veldkamp
a435.title: Dutch Minister of Foreign Affairs
a435.speech: Declared that if Israel does not fulfil its humanitarian obligations, the Netherlands will push for the suspension of the trade part of the association agreement between the EU and Israel.

a435.speaker: Several EU member states, including Germany
a435.name: Several EU member states
a435.title: including Germany
a435.speech: Insist on Israel's right to defend itself, in accordance with international law.

a435.speaker: Other EU member states, such as Spain
a435.name: Other EU member states
a435.title: such as Spain
a435.speech: Denounce the "genocide" against the Palestinians in Gaza.

a435.speaker: European Commission report presented to the 27 member states at the end of June
a435.name: European Commission report presented to the 27 member states at the end of June
a435.speech: Concluded that Israel was violating an article of the association agreement between the country and the EU relating to respect for human rights.

a435.speaker: European Commission (proposal presented on Monday)
a435.name: European Commission (proposal presented on Monday)
a435.speech: Proposed the partial suspension of Israel's participation in the major Horizon Europe research programme, specifically targeting start-ups specialising in cybersecurity, drones and artificial intelligence.

a524.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a524.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a524.speech: According to UNHCR, more than 20 million people are forcibly displaced by weather related sudden onset hazards each year and 12 million of them are from Africa.

a524.speaker: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
a524.name: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
a524.speech: According to an intergovernmental panel on climate change (IPCC), agriculture accounts for about 75% of the labor force.

a524.speaker: CNN
a524.name: CNN
a524.speech: As CNN indicated, on March 2017, more than 100 people died in Somalia in 48 hours.

a524.speaker: UN assessment
a524.name: UN assessment
a524.speech: The UN assessment estimates that 4.7 million people - nearly 40% of Somalia's population - are in need of humanitarian assistance.

a542.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.name: Atupele Muluzi
a542.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.speech: Has raised alarm over what he describes as a growing threat to democracy in Malawi, warning that the country is on a dangerous path toward autocratic rule and internal decay; told fellow leaders at the Platform for African Democrats (PAD) conference in Angola that Malawi is experiencing a rollback of democratic principles amid rising global instability and weakening international cooperation: "We are witnessing a dangerous shift: a retreat from the principles that have long underpinned democratic governance. Truth itself has become a casualty, with disinformation distorting the foundations of informed political discourse."

a542.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.name: Atupele Muluzi
a542.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.speech: Pointed to the consolidation of power by autocratic regimes across the continent, adding that such trends have emboldened leaders who undermine democracy through coercion rather than consent, and accused the current administration of using undemocratic tactics to cling to power: "The current administration has failed to deliver on its economic and social promises. Facing near-certain electoral defeat, it is resorting to undemocratic means to maintain control." ; urged Malawians to resist any attempts to subvert democratic norms.

a542.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.name: Atupele Muluzi
a542.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.speech: Highlighted the impact of shrinking international support, citing the scaling back of donor agencies such as USAID, and warned that Africa is being left to tackle economic stagnation, agricultural insecurity, corruption, and poor governance largely on its own: "Yet, this is precisely when we need greater collaboration to tackle Africa's pressing challenges."

a542.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.name: Atupele Muluzi
a542.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.speech: Accused several African governments of falling prey to kleptocracy, describing them as "government by the corrupt, for the corrupt," where leaders prioritize personal enrichment over public service.

a542.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.name: Atupele Muluzi
a542.title: United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
a542.speech: Called on Malawians to speak with a united voice to defend the country's democracy: "This is our moment to stand firm for democracy. We cannot allow our democracy to be stolen."

a542.speaker: Malawi government officials
a542.name: Malawi government officials
a542.speech: Did not immediately respond to Muluzi's claims.

a581.speaker: Nam Waya Rahouf Ouedraogo, head of the TERIATEL project delegation
a581.name: Nam Waya Rahouf Ouedraogo
a581.title: head of the TERIATEL project delegation
a581.speech: "We came to present our project to the minister. It is a project to set up a mobile telephone network, called TERIATEL" ; specified that "the objective is to offer concrete and reliable telecommunications solutions to the three countries of the Alliance of Sahel States, and more particularly to Burkina Faso."

a581.speaker: Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabane, Minister of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications
a581.name: Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabane
a581.title: Minister of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications
a581.speech: Welcomed their approach and promised to organise working sessions with the technical services of her department to better understand the details of the project.

a814.speaker: Dr David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa, President of the Society for AIDS in Africa
a814.name: Dr David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa
a814.title: President of the Society for AIDS in Africa
a814.speech: Recently warned that without innovative approaches to sustainable domestic financing, Africa risked regressing to the dark days of the 1980s and 1990s when many died from AIDS due to the lack of medicine; consequently called on Africans and the diaspora to rise to the challenge of strengthening health systems with accountability, transparency and universal access to care ; “Given the recent action taken by the US government to freeze funding for HIV support, it is crucial that as we work within our respective committees, we address the domestic financing of health systems and the sustainability of our HIV/AIDS response,” Dr Parirenyatwa stated at the conference in Accra.

a814.speaker: World Health Organisation (data cited)
a814.name: World Health Organisation (data cited)
a814.speech: In 2022, the World Health Organisation African Region had 25.6 million people living with HIV, with about 380,000 people dying from AIDS-related illnesses.

a867.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a867.name: John Dramani Mahama
a867.title: President of Ghana
a867.speech: Has announced that the 24-Hour Economy policy promised by the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC) during the 2024 electioneering campaign will officially take effect from July 1, 2025 ; described the policy as a “game-changing strategy” aimed at unlocking Ghana’s full production potential ; “We are also implementing a game-changing strategy, which is the 24-hour economy, to unlock Ghana’s production potential across all sectors. I am pleased to announce that from July 1, the 24-hour Economy policy will be ready to go into operation.”

a867.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a867.name: John Dramani Mahama
a867.title: President of Ghana
a867.speech: Further explained the critical role the policy will play in strengthening the horticulture industry by facilitating the smooth movement of perishable goods such as pineapples, vegetables, and herbs from farms to international markets; according to him, the round-the-clock operations would reduce post-harvest losses and increase export value ; “This policy will provide the framework for continued production, processing, and logistics in horticulture. It allows perishable goods like pineapple, vegetables, and herbs to move swiftly from the field to international shelves, thereby minimising losses and maximising value.”

a867.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a867.name: John Dramani Mahama
a867.title: President of Ghana
a867.speech: Revealed that his government is working with key stakeholders to extend 24-hour operations to Ghana’s two major ports ; “I am pleased to inform you that the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Agri-business and the Ministry of Transport are working together with the GRA, Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority, Ghana Shippers’ Council, and other stakeholders to soon declare Tema and Takoradi ports as 24-hour ports.”

a887.speaker: Isam Karrar, Sudanese Ambassador to South Sudan
a887.name: Isam Karrar
a887.title: Sudanese Ambassador to South Sudan
a887.speech: Announced that his government has opened humanitarian corridors to facilitate relief efforts and deliver aid to millions of civilians in need nationwide, as long as it is done without any hidden agenda that serves interests contrary to Sudan’s sovereignty ; said his government has approved about 100 movement permits to the United Nations agencies and international NGOs providing aid to the displaced population, which enabled UN agencies to provide thousands of tons of food supplies and life-saving medicines to the people ; “Sudan is completely open to providing humanitarian assistance to all displaced persons and refugees in Sudan. Also approved about 100 movement permits have been issued to UN agencies such as the World Food Program, the High Commissioner for Refugees, the International Organization for Migration, and the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs” ; “All of this indicates Sudan’s openness and is in line with the main priority of the Sudanese government to facilitate humanitarian work for all parties committed to humanitarian work only without implementing an agenda for that” ; “The UN agencies have provided thousands of tons of food supplies and thousands of tons of life-saving medicines and children’s medicines to several states in Sudan.”

a887.speaker: Isam Karrar, Sudanese Ambassador to South Sudan
a887.name: Isam Karrar
a887.title: Sudanese Ambassador to South Sudan
a887.speech: Highlighted the change of President Salva Kiir as the chairman of an IGAD committee to steer the peace process that caused the stalemate: “Sudan remains with its people and the government welcomes all the initiatives that aim to achieve peace without presenting a hidden agenda that can serve interests which always oppose the sovereign of Sudan” ; “Sudan agreed since the beginning of the war to sit and start Jeddah talks in Saudi Arabia, and all the decisions that came as a result of those talks” ; “Sudan also agreed on the IGAD initiatives to solve the Sudanese crisis and when we started entering the primary talks” ; “IGAD changed the chairman who was the president of the republic of South Sudan His Excellency Salva Kiir Mayardit, who was commissioned in the beginning in the Sudanese crisis file, the IGAD changed him with the president of Kenya and Sudan and its people refused this step.”

a887.speaker: United Nations
a887.name: United Nations
a887.speech: According to the UN, at least 20,000 people have been killed, but the death toll is likely to be much higher due to the ongoing fighting and the collapse of the health system ; the UN also said in early October that famine and the outbreak of diseases like cholera have further exacerbated an already desperate situation.

a976.speaker: Ter Manyang, Executive Director of Center for Peace and Advocacy (CPA)
a976.name: Ter Manyang
a976.title: Executive Director of Center for Peace and Advocacy (CPA)
a976.speech: Told President Salva Kiir and First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar that South Sudan cannot afford another civil war, urging the country’s leadership to choose political dialogue to resolve differences; said Kiir and Machar should think twice about resorting to military confrontations, and instead address the current tensions through direct meetings. “As a human rights activist, I urge President Salva Kiir and First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar to choose dialogue and engage in face-to-face discussions rather than resorting to military solutions,” he said in a WhatsApp voice note shared with Eye Radio on Tuesday. ; “The relative peace we currently have in the country is better than nothing. South Sudan cannot afford to go back to full-scale war.”

a976.speaker: Ter Manyang, Executive Director of Center for Peace and Advocacy (CPA)
a976.name: Ter Manyang
a976.title: Executive Director of Center for Peace and Advocacy (CPA)
a976.speech: Said top leaders have a direct responsibility to foster peace, adding that it is time for South Sudanese leaders to prioritize national interests over their personal gains.

a976.speaker: Ter Manyang, Executive Director of Center for Peace and Advocacy (CPA)
a976.name: Ter Manyang
a976.title: Executive Director of Center for Peace and Advocacy (CPA)
a976.speech: Called upon the international community, the African Union, UNMISS, and other partners to intervene in the current situation.

a1031.speaker: Wellington Takavarasha, President of the Zimbabwe Artisanal and Small Scale for Sustainable Mining Council
a1031.name: Wellington Takavarasha
a1031.title: President of the Zimbabwe Artisanal and Small Scale for Sustainable Mining Council
a1031.speech: “The prices have been very favourable to the miners, which is something we are so happy about” ; “This year is looking very good. We must capitalise on this rally.”

a1031.speaker: Ethiopia's central bank
a1031.name: Ethiopia's central bank
a1031.speech: said record deliveries of the metal are boosting its reserves.

a1031.speaker: Goldman Sachs
a1031.name: Goldman Sachs
a1031.speech: forecast the gold price will reach $3,700 by year end.

a1031.speaker: Mxolisi Dube, artisanal gold miner in Filabusi
a1031.name: Mxolisi Dube
a1031.title: artisanal gold miner in Filabusi
a1031.speech: “You are assured of getting something at the end of the month” ; “You are protected. If you are not under a company you always have to run away.”

a1031.speaker: Mxolisi Dube, artisanal gold miner in Filabusi
a1031.name: Mxolisi Dube
a1031.title: artisanal gold miner in Filabusi
a1031.speech: “The high prices mean in the near future I will also be seen in a car. I want a Toyota Hilux 4×4, with a 2.7-litre engine.”

a1031.speaker: Meli Nkulumo, plant manager at Macoomber 7 mine
a1031.name: Meli Nkulumo
a1031.title: plant manager at Macoomber 7 mine
a1031.speech: “This means we always have ore available and are milling more.”

a1031.speaker: Thulani Ndlovu, acting mine manager at Macoomber 7 mine
a1031.name: Thulani Ndlovu
a1031.title: acting mine manager at Macoomber 7 mine
a1031.speech: “Higher gold prices are better for everyone. We can also look forward to a raise in salaries.”

a1031.speaker: Thabo Mpofu, manager of Next Generation bar
a1031.name: Thabo Mpofu
a1031.title: manager of Next Generation bar
a1031.speech: said drinking holes are busy with “all sorts of people” spending big, adding that he has seen clients buy bottles of Hennessey Cognac and pour them out on the ground as a show of wealth.

a1031.speaker: Melusi Nyoni, manager of Fred and Fernando mines
a1031.name: Melusi Nyoni
a1031.title: manager of Fred and Fernando mines
a1031.speech: “There's nothing bad that happens here” ; “There is gold just all over.”

a1031.speaker: Chamber of Mines (last annual report)
a1031.name: Chamber of Mines (last annual report)
a1031.speech: said informal miners accounted for 87% of the 186 deaths in Zimbabwean mining accidents.

a1031.speaker: Local media reports
a1031.name: Local media reports
a1031.speech: reported that four miners died at a mine near Chegutu in northern Zimbabwe in late May when a wall of earth collapsed onto them.

a1066.speaker: EU delegation in Nigeria (statement)
a1066.name: EU delegation in Nigeria (statement)
a1066.speech: In a statement on Thursday, said the funding will be used to provide cash support for the victims as well as water, sanitation, healthcare, psychosocial support and essential household items.

a1066.speaker: European Commission
a1066.name: European Commission
a1066.speech: According to the commission, the funding is part of its contribution to the Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC); it also noted that the fund, through the IFRC, would ensure the provision of life-saving humanitarian assistance to 2,500 vulnerable households displaced in the last four months in both states. "Beyond immediate relief, the initiative will strengthen protection services and conduct awareness campaigns on health, hygiene, and safety. This comprehensive approach aims to not only alleviate suffering but also to safeguard the dignity of vulnerable people - especially women, children, and those repeatedly displaced - who are now living in precarious, overcrowded, and underserved conditions."

a1066.speaker: Amnesty International
a1066.name: Amnesty International
a1066.speech: There are currently more than 15,000 internally displaced persons in Benue State, according to Amnesty International.

a1066.speaker: European Commission / European Union
a1066.name: European Commission / European Union
a1066.speech: The commission had also earlier noted that it had no plan to scale down on humanitarian assistance to vulnerable communities in the country; the union rejected claims that it made a massive funding cut to humanitarian assistance, describing them as "unsubstantiated" and "inaccurate."

a1176.speaker: Anthony Myers, Acting Finance and Development Planning Minister of Liberia
a1176.name: Anthony Myers
a1176.title: Acting Finance and Development Planning Minister of Liberia
a1176.speech: On behalf of the Government of Liberia, described the endeavor as a roadmap that has so many positives for Liberia and the government in various dimensions, while pointing out the significance of the project with respect to the Government's ARREST Agenda for inclusive Development (AAID). Mr. Myers stated that at the policy level and given the project's largely solar energy-based composition, this will help the government meet its key international obligations, including environmental and carbon targets, as it will have less environmental impact while boosting trade, local business development, investment, and security and mitigating crimes. He noted that everyone is aware that the southeastern region of Liberia has been marginalized not as a deliberate act of some politicians or influential group, but due to geographic isolation, outlining that the region has been left behind in terms of infrastructural development, roads, electricity and economy opportunities ; "So, with respect to inclusion, the Government of Liberia having an inclusive agenda to give balanced development across the country, the Global Gateway and the EU funding this project is helping the government to achieve that goal, and we want to say thanks to our Development Partners. We are grateful for this project because it will uncork some of the key binding constrains the region is facing." ; described Electricity as a critical tool for kick-starting economic progress and sectorial growth, arguing that the ARREST Agenda is not achievable without Electricity and the Southeast region has all those listed in the ARREST Agenda, especially tourism.

a1176.speaker: Thomas Zailee Gonkerwon, Acting Managing Director of the Liberia Electricity Corporation
a1176.name: Thomas Zailee Gonkerwon
a1176.title: Acting Managing Director of the Liberia Electricity Corporation
a1176.speech: Expressed contentment about the meeting and praised all the Stakeholders, calling on the parties to continue their commitment to the Rural Electrification Project, moving forward.

a1176.speaker: Nona Deprez, European Union Ambassador to Liberia
a1176.name: Nona Deprez
a1176.title: European Union Ambassador to Liberia
a1176.speech: Expressed excitement and appreciation for the first steering committee meeting, describing it as a milestone and step to addressing electricity challenge and minimizing environmental waste and pollution through solar energy ; "This Project costs 42 million Euros and it will be implemented in the counties listed. We are doing this to help health facilities and businesses in those counties. I hope that everyone will respect the set deadline. The European Union and Liberia shared a very common development interest and with this government in many sectors but particularly in the Energy Sector with regards to this project. Meeting here today, I'm really proud to announce that recently we have successfully completed a new project of US$52 million Euro for Transmission and Distribution of Electricity, ensuring 42,000 households in greater Monrovia have access to electricity."

a1176.speaker: Samuel Nagbe, Executive Director of the Rural and Renewable Energy Agency (RREA)
a1176.name: Samuel Nagbe
a1176.title: Executive Director of the Rural and Renewable Energy Agency (RREA)
a1176.speech: Expressed appreciation to the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP), the European Union, among others, for the round-table meeting ; "This is going to allow us now to finally make sure that citizens in the targeted counties finally have access to electricity. It's also important that we stress that under Article 2.2 of the Financing Agreement, it clearly states that 'All the funds disbursed by the Commission are exempt from covering operations costs, especially for those that we are involved with. Also, under this Agreement, the Government commits that they will cover those costs.'"

a1223.speaker: Ken Alew Gebrekristos, 38, metal welder displaced from Edaga Arbi, Tigray
a1223.name: Ken Alew Gebrekristos
a1223.title: 38, metal welder displaced from Edaga Arbi, Tigray
a1223.speech: "So far we have been given some injera (flatbreads) and T-shirts." ; "We fetched water from the river to drink. Some days we ate nothing. One girl who was displaced with us gave birth, with no doctor around. We had just a bedsheet to offer them, so we made a fire to warm up the baby." ; With tears in his eyes and his voice breaking: "Now I have no plans, no idea what my immediate future looks like. I can't go back home – how could I go back without guarantees? I feel safer here surrounded by other people."

a1223.speaker: People staying at the Basin school site in Axum (displaced people)
a1223.name: People staying at the Basin school site in Axum (displaced people)
a1223.speech: Say the movement of people is constant, but the influx has intensified since early March.

a1223.speaker: Bayesh Danyo, 25, displaced mother of two from Humera, western Tigray
a1223.name: Bayesh Danyo
a1223.title: 25, displaced mother of two from Humera, western Tigray
a1223.speech: "I've been here for 42 days now." ; "At the beginning I got five litres of cooking oil, 30 kg of flour and 50 kg of wheat. These are all about to run out. The few food distributions that happen are not always fair. I try to share whatever I have with other newcomers, particularly pregnant women." ; "We haven't really had a chance to wash ourselves since we arrived. My baby gets sick because of the harsh conditions in which we sleep."

a1223.speaker: Inhabitants of towns including Humera, Dansha and Mai Kadra
a1223.name: Inhabitants of towns including Humera
a1223.title: Dansha and Mai Kadra
a1223.speech: Claim to have been pressurised by militias and armed groups to leave their hometowns and sometimes to have been forcibly put into buses which dropped them on the far side of the Tekeze river.

a1223.speaker: Other displaced people from western Tigray
a1223.name: Other displaced people from western Tigray
a1223.speech: Say that they experienced and witnessed violence of various types which made the decision to leave unavoidable.

a1223.speaker: Esperanza Santos, MSF emergency coordinator in Tigray
a1223.name: Esperanza Santos
a1223.title: MSF emergency coordinator in Tigray
a1223.speech: "We have seen displacement happening since the beginning of the crisis, but people were not displacing in such big numbers and those who had to leave their houses were often supported by host communities, staying mostly in the houses of relatives or of people they knew and sharing resources with them." ; "Recently this has changed and we are seeing a bigger influx of people, especially in Shire, Adwa and Axum. Most are settling in informal sites that don't have the capacity to host this number of people and that lack services for them. It is an extremely concerning situation because we are not seeing an adequate response from the humanitarian community to address people's need for water, sanitation, food or medical services."

a1223.speaker: Worku, 22, former clothes shop owner displaced to Abi Adi
a1223.name: Worku
a1223.title: 22, former clothes shop owner displaced to Abi Adi
a1223.speech: "I finally came to Abi Adi because there is more presence of humanitarian organisations. Over the past few months, I had to beg from local people. At the most, I received an injera each day. I need food, clothes, water, shelter... Everywhere I've been, I've been sleeping on the ground. Health-wise I am still fine, but I have seen others get sick on the way and die."

a1223.speaker: Leterbrahn, displaced young woman from Humera
a1223.name: Leterbrahn
a1223.title: displaced young woman from Humera
a1223.speech: Says she has lost almost everything she owned. "I only have the clothes you see here. I can't even cook for myself as I don't have any utensils. I don't even own a blanket. At one point I was given four bedsheets by local people, but I gave them to the pregnant women. We feel forgotten by the international community and the Ethiopian government. Nobody reaches us. Even after such a long time, we have nothing."

a1223.speaker: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a1223.name: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a1223.speech: MSF teams are rehabilitating a number of health facilities across the Tigray region and providing them with drugs and other medical supplies, as well as providing hands-on medical support in emergency rooms, maternity wards and outpatient departments. MSF teams are also running mobile clinics in rural towns and villages where the health system is not functioning, and in informal sites where displaced people are staying. However, there are still rural areas in Tigray that neither MSF, nor any other organisation, has been able to reach; MSF can only assume that people living in these areas are also without access to healthcare. In response to this wave of newly arrived internally displaced people, MSF is also focusing on water and sanitation activities in some of the main towns.

a1542.speaker: Emmanuel Robert Gborlee, vendor at Duala Market
a1542.name: Emmanuel Robert Gborlee
a1542.title: vendor at Duala Market
a1542.speech: "I am not feeling good about this dirt. We don't have any sitting area to sell, so we are forced to sit on the road" ; "Every day, we pay, but still, the dirt stays here. It has been here for more than four days. We want the government to help us clear the streets."

a1542.speaker: Emmanuel Robert Gborlee, vendor at Duala Market
a1542.name: Emmanuel Robert Gborlee
a1542.title: vendor at Duala Market
a1542.speech: Notes the paradox that while authorities are quick to enforce street vending regulations - and police officers readily chase vendors off the roads to maintain order - waste collection remains slow and irregular.

a1542.speaker: Alex Tamba, vendor who has worked at Duala Market for over a decade
a1542.name: Alex Tamba
a1542.title: vendor who has worked at Duala Market for over a decade
a1542.speech: Describes an unprecedented deterioration in conditions: "This is not how the place used to be. Nowhere for us to sell, so we sit near the dirt. Sometimes we even pay 'zoogos' to carry the dirt away, but it still stays for a long time before MCC comes. We want the government to relocate the dumpsite away from the market."

a1542.speaker: Annieta Kromah, long-time market seller at Duala Market
a1542.name: Annieta Kromah
a1542.title: long-time market seller at Duala Market
a1542.speech: "We pay 50LD every day, but the places we sell are full of dirt. We even get sick from it. I want the City Mayor to employ more manpower to clean the streets."

a1542.speaker: Fombah B. Swaray, market observer
a1542.name: Fombah B. Swaray
a1542.title: market observer
a1542.speech: Observes: "The accumulation of dirt in the market has forced sellers into the streets, resulting in traffic congestion."

a1542.speaker: Fombah B. Swaray, market observer
a1542.name: Fombah B. Swaray
a1542.title: market observer
a1542.speech: Suggests looking to the past for solutions: "I want the City Mayor to put a program together like student vacation work, the way Mary Broh did. Every Saturday, students used to clean the streets. We also need a strong task force to fine people who throw dirt on the streets."

a1542.speaker: Clinton Nyumah, market user
a1542.name: Clinton Nyumah
a1542.title: market user
a1542.speech: Points out that sanitation infrastructure has eroded over time: "During President Ellen Johnson's time, there were pit latrines on the streets for citizens to use, and sweepers collected the waste. We need that system back. The government must launch awareness campaigns and enforce fines on people who throw dirt on the streets."

a1542.speaker: Jonathan Massaquoi, market user
a1542.name: Jonathan Massaquoi
a1542.title: market user
a1542.speech: Proposes a collaborative approach that includes all stakeholders, even the marginalized: "The dirt is embarrassing us. We want the Mayor to employ 'zoogos' because they are hardworking people who can help keep the city clean. But strong measures must also be put in place to punish those who drop dirt carelessly."

a1545.speaker: A group of 169 aid organisations (joint statement)
a1545.name: A group of 169 aid organisations (joint statement)
a1545.speech: Called for an end to a US- and Israeli-backed aid distribution scheme in Gaza and urged a return to the UN-led aid mechanism: "NGOs call for immediate action to end the deadly Israeli distribution scheme (including the so-called Gaza Humanitarian Foundation) in Gaza" ; urged action to "revert to the existing UN-led coordination mechanisms, and lift the Israeli government's blockade on aid and commercial supplies" ; "Under the Israeli government's new scheme, starved and weakened civilians are being forced to trek for hours through dangerous terrain and active conflict zones, only to face a violent, chaotic race to reach fenced, militarized distribution sites." They said more than 500 Palestinians were killed and almost 4,000 injured while trying to access or distribute food in less than four weeks.

a1545.speaker: Health ministry of the Hamas-ruled territory of Gaza
a1545.name: Health ministry of the Hamas-ruled territory of Gaza
a1545.speech: Has given similar figures for the number of Palestinians killed and injured while trying to access or distribute food.

a1545.speaker: Israel (government position)
a1545.name: Israel (government position)
a1545.speech: Said it tasked the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation with distribution in Gaza to keep Hamas from controlling the flow of aid.

a1545.speaker: The Israeli military
a1545.name: The Israeli military
a1545.speech: Last week denied a newspaper report that cited Israeli soldiers as saying they had been ordered to fire at civilians near aid centres.

a1545.speaker: Israeli soldiers cited in a newspaper report (anonymous)
a1545.name: Israeli soldiers cited in a newspaper report (anonymous)
a1545.speech: Said they had been ordered to fire at civilians near aid centres.

a1559.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a1559.name: Experts (unnamed)
a1559.speech: Warn that without urgent intervention, up to 4 million more people could die annually in Africa from preventable and treatable diseases, pushing health standards back to the early 2000s.

a1559.speaker: Dr. Jean Kaseya, Director-General of Africa CDC (statement released January 31, 2025)
a1559.name: Dr. Jean Kaseya
a1559.title: Director-General of Africa CDC (statement released January 31, 2025)
a1559.speech: Warned: “This is not just an African problem; it is a global crisis in the making. We are at risk of losing everything we fought for over the past two decades.”

a1559.speaker: Dr. Jean Kaseya, Director-General of Africa CDC
a1559.name: Dr. Jean Kaseya
a1559.title: Director-General of Africa CDC
a1559.speech: On the crisis in Goma and eastern DRC: “I will personally fly there to ensure these life-saving interventions reach those in need—but we must have safe access.”

a1559.speaker: Dr. Jean Kaseya, Director-General of Africa CDC
a1559.name: Dr. Jean Kaseya
a1559.title: Director-General of Africa CDC
a1559.speech: Emphasized that although Africa CDC has successfully lobbied for a waiver on humanitarian aid, aid alone will not be enough and the region's leaders must act decisively to end conflicts that are fuelling disease outbreaks: “To my fellow African leaders: End this unnecessary war. If you fail to act, it will not be bullets that kill us—it will be major outbreaks and pandemics emerging from this region, devastating economies and sparing no one.”

a1602.speaker: AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) and other Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) in Nigeria
a1602.name: AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) and other Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) in Nigeria
a1602.speech: Have called for local financing for HIV and tuberculosis (TB).

a1602.speaker: Network of People Living With HIV/AIDS In Nigeria (NEPWHAN)
a1602.name: Network of People Living With HIV/AIDS In Nigeria (NEPWHAN)
a1602.speech: Harped on the need for domestication of the anti-stigma, discrimination law.

a1602.speaker: Abuja Declaration of 2001 (African Union member states commitment document)
a1602.name: Abuja Declaration of 2001 (African Union member states commitment document)
a1602.speech: A commitment by African Union member states to increase their annual health budgets to at least 15 percent of their national budget to combat HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria; the declaration also urged developed countries to meet their target of providing 0.7 percent of their Gross National Product (GNP) as official development assistance (ODA) to developing nations.

a1602.speaker: Participants at the CSO Financing event
a1602.name: Participants at the CSO Financing event
a1602.speech: Said that, with the recent pullback by global donors, the parliament needs to revisit how the Abuja declaration might come into effect.

a1602.speaker: Abdul Kadir Ibrahim, National Coordinator of NEPWHAN
a1602.name: Abdul Kadir Ibrahim
a1602.title: National Coordinator of NEPWHAN
a1602.speech: Said it is pertinent for stakeholders to see how the nation can mobilise local resources for AIDS, TB and Malaria and for states across the country to revisit the HIV anti-stigma and discrimination law to be domesticated by state Houses of Assemblies ; "The US government's policy shift has really given us the kind of strong signal that we need to look inward and also see how we could identify internal resources to accommodate and finance our health progress, most especially HIV, which has to do with our community members." ; "Currently, about 80 to 85 per cent of HIV funding is being supported through foreign aid, especially with a large chunk from the US government and also about 35 per cent from the Global Fund and other funding sources. In all these, there is less than 15 per cent from the government of Nigeria." ; said that to ensure progress there is a need to capture people in the National Health Insurance Scheme and also ensure sustainability.

a1846.speaker: United Nations
a1846.name: United Nations
a1846.speech: Says 25 million people need humanitarian assistance in Sudan, and about 18 million are faced with acute hunger in the region.

a1846.speaker: Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED)
a1846.name: Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED)
a1846.speech: Reported that since the start of the conflict, there have been "5 550 events of political violence and more than 15 550 reported fatalities", with the most recorded violence in Khartoum, with more than 3 660 events and over 7 050 fatalities.

a1846.speaker: Samantha Power, United States Agency for International Development administrator (statement)
a1846.name: Samantha Power
a1846.title: United States Agency for International Development administrator (statement)
a1846.speech: Revealed how some communities had been almost wiped out or exposed to horrific incidents that would last for generations.

a1846.speaker: Amir Suliman, African Centre for Justice and Peace Studies (ACJPS)
a1846.name: Amir Suliman
a1846.title: African Centre for Justice and Peace Studies (ACJPS)
a1846.speech: Told News24 that Sudan was on its knees: "The war is now hurting more people. There are now many other militias taking sides in the war. The Islamists too are seeing it as an opportunity to take over. The war is almost countrywide, it has moved beyond Darfur, Khartoum and other places. ; All of this is happening as the international community watches. They are not putting enough pressure to stop the war. What we want from the international community is to put sanctions on both factions."

a1846.speaker: Abdel-Fattah Burhan's government
a1846.name: Abdel-Fattah Burhan's government
a1846.speech: Is opposed to the International Humanitarian Conference for Sudan hosted by France because it impinges on "the affairs of Sudan... without consultation or coordination with its government and its participation".

a1846.speaker: General Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, Rapid Support Forces (RSF) leader
a1846.name: General Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo
a1846.title: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) leader
a1846.speech: Addressed the world, blaming the war on the SAF and the former government of deposed leader Omar al-Bashir. He said his army was committed to peace and wanted an investigation into war crimes. He referred to the SAF as "heroic soldiers" who only fought to defend themselves.

a1846.speaker: RSF spokesperson's office (statement)
a1846.name: RSF spokesperson's office (statement)
a1846.speech: "Our courageous soldiers secured a decisive victory, establishing full control over Mellit. The RSF successfully captured 46 fully equipped military vehicles, detained 70 mercenaries, and liberated camps previously held by the Gibril, Minawi, and Tambour movements. ; Our forces are now diligently pursuing those who fled the battlefield, taking charge of their prisoners and casualties."

a1846.speaker: World Food Programme (@WFP post on X, citing @WFPChief)
a1846.name: World Food Programme (@WFP post on X
a1846.title: citing @WFPChief)
a1846.speech: "With fighting only intensifying, the impacts of #Sudan's war are reverberating around the entire region. The fighting must stop now, or the region may soon become the world's largest hunger crisis, @WFPChief has warned."

a1846.speaker: General Abdel-Fattah Burhan, de facto head of state and head of the Sudanese Armed Forces
a1846.name: General Abdel-Fattah Burhan
a1846.title: de facto head of state and head of the Sudanese Armed Forces
a1846.speech: Said last week he was not in a position to negotiate with the RSF, which he branded a terrorist outfit.

a1846.speaker: The Guardian
a1846.name: The Guardian
a1846.speech: Reported that the UK government was holding secret talks with the RSF.

a1846.speaker: Rights groups
a1846.name: Rights groups
a1846.speech: Warned that the UK's secret talks with the RSF could risk "legitimising the notorious militia - which continues to commit multiple war crimes - while undermining Britain's moral credibility in the region".

a1863.speaker: Office of the Treasury Registrar (OTR), Tanzania
a1863.name: Office of the Treasury Registrar (OTR)
a1863.title: Tanzania
a1863.speech: Has announced that it surpassed its Non-Tax Revenue (NTR) collection target from Public and Statutory Corporations (PSCs) and minority interests (MIs) by an impressive 205 per cent in February.

a1863.speaker: Nehemiah Mchechu, Treasury Registrar
a1863.name: Nehemiah Mchechu
a1863.title: Treasury Registrar
a1863.speech: Attributed this success to the supportive policies established under the fifth-phase regime of President Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan: "The policies implemented have allowed PSCs and MIs to operate efficiently, enabling them to scale up their contributions to the government's coffers." ; "The government's focus on operational excellence and commercial viability is crucial," noting that his office oversees 308 PSCs and MIs ; "We need to assess how to grow each funding source more consistently to significantly increase contributions to the Consolidated Fund."

a1863.speaker: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
a1863.name: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
a1863.speech: Pointing out that NTR remains an underutilised resource.

a2215.speaker: Niger (government)
a2215.name: Niger (government)
a2215.speech: Deemed its military cooperation agreement with the United States "illegal," leading the US military to close its last base in Niger in August.

a2215.speaker: Ethiopia (government)
a2215.name: Ethiopia (government)
a2215.speech: In May described the US ambassador's speech on its internal affairs as "unsolicited advice."

a2215.speaker: Gallup global leadership perception survey
a2215.name: Gallup global leadership perception survey
a2215.speech: According to the latest Gallup survey on the perception of global leadership, the median approval rating of the United States in Africa, an indicator of the country's soft power, fell from 59% in 2022 to 56% in 2023; of the four major countries surveyed, the United States is the only one whose image in Africa did not improve in 2023.

a2215.speaker: US Census Bureau
a2215.name: US Census Bureau
a2215.speech: According to the US Census Bureau, trade between the United States and Africa, which stood at $113 billion in 2010, contracted to $67.4 billion in 2023.

a2215.speaker: Statista (global data and business intelligence platform)
a2215.name: Statista (global data and business intelligence platform)
a2215.speech: According to Statista, after a peak of $69 billion in 2014, US foreign direct investment in Africa fell to $44.81 billion in 2020 before reaching $56.29 billion in 2023.

a2215.speaker: Cameron Hudson, Senior Fellow of the Africa Program at CSIS (Center for Strategic and International Studies)
a2215.name: Cameron Hudson
a2215.title: Senior Fellow of the Africa Program at CSIS (Center for Strategic and International Studies)
a2215.speech: Said in a CSIS report: "While the US-led response to climate change, development financing and great-power competition seems to continue to favour the Global North (...), this over-promising and lack of results have only reinforced the well-established reputation that Washington is an inherently unreliable, even hypocritical, partner."

a2215.speaker: William Ruto, Kenyan President
a2215.name: William Ruto
a2215.title: Kenyan President
a2215.speech: Was indignant at the unceremonious reception at the 2022 US-Africa summit, where more than 50 African leaders were bused to the venue, and denounced the impropriety of "packing us into buses like schoolchildren."

a2215.speaker: Arikana Chihombori-Quao, former African Union representative to the United States
a2215.name: Arikana Chihombori-Quao
a2215.title: former African Union representative to the United States
a2215.speech: "The US-Africa summit (will be) a failure if the Americans do not treat Africans as equals" ; "historically, the United States has regarded Africa as its 'backyard' and has practised racial discrimination against Africans."

a2215.speaker: Seco Cassama, Bissau-Guinean political scientist
a2215.name: Seco Cassama
a2215.title: Bissau-Guinean political scientist
a2215.speech: Said the United States completely ignores African reality: "its traditions, its civilisations — it always imposes its interests above those of Africans," and stated that the American initiative is often an imposition that does not respect African reality.

a2215.speaker: Olayinka Ajala, lecturer in politics and international relations at Leeds Beckett University (UK)
a2215.name: Olayinka Ajala
a2215.title: lecturer in politics and international relations at Leeds Beckett University (UK)
a2215.speech: According to his data analysis, despite the US operation that began in 2013, terrorist activity and deaths have continued to rise since 2014, with attacks increasing significantly since 2018 when the United States opened Air Base 201 in Agadez, highlighting the ineffectiveness of American strategies, which take no account of local realities or of the sentiments of the population.

a2215.speaker: Fred M'membe, president of the Socialist Party of Zambia
a2215.name: Fred M'membe
a2215.title: president of the Socialist Party of Zambia
a2215.speech: During US Vice-President Kamala Harris's visit to Africa in March 2023, accused the United States of having orchestrated coups d'état, overthrown several governments and assassinated African leaders: "Today, such a country comes to teach us what democracy is."

a2215.speaker: Ibrahima Diao, Senegalese academic specialising in international relations
a2215.name: Ibrahima Diao
a2215.title: Senegalese academic specialising in international relations
a2215.speech: "In most of their infrastructure projects in developing countries, the United States imposes its democratic values."

a2215.speaker: The Herald newspaper (Zimbabwe)
a2215.name: The Herald newspaper (Zimbabwe)
a2215.speech: Points out that the United States uses its superpower status and economic power to intimidate other countries, in a display of authority and arrogance that offends Africa.

a2234.speaker: Abdul Kamara, Director General of the African Development Bank's Nigeria Office
a2234.name: Abdul Kamara
a2234.title: Director General of the African Development Bank's Nigeria Office
a2234.speech: "This investment illustrates our commitment to continue working with the Government to fill critical infrastructure gaps in Nigeria's health system while building resilient, climate-adapted healthcare facilities." ; "By strengthening healthcare infrastructure in Sokoto State, we are building hope and creating pathways to better health outcomes for millions of Nigerians."

a2234.speaker: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the African Development Bank Group (AfDB)
a2234.name: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the African Development Bank Group (AfDB)
a2234.speech: According to it, the African Development Bank Group remains committed to enhancing the quality of life for Africa's people through targeted investments in resilient health infrastructure that drive inclusive growth and sustainable development across the continent.

a2325.speaker: Rogerio Zandamela, Governor of the Bank of Mozambique
a2325.name: Rogerio Zandamela
a2325.title: Governor of the Bank of Mozambique
a2325.speech: Put forward the position, this Monday in Maputo after the meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee, that at this moment there is no need to resume direct financing of fuel imports, despite the pressures being felt in international supply.

a2325.speaker: Government of Mozambique, private sector and OTM trade union confederation
a2325.name: Government of Mozambique
a2325.title: private sector and OTM trade union confederation
a2325.speech: Fear that the effects of the war in the Middle East and the unfavourable economic situation will influence the setting of the new national minimum wage.

a2325.speaker: Feizal Sidat, President of the Mozambican Football Federation
a2325.name: Feizal Sidat
a2325.title: President of the Mozambican Football Federation
a2325.speech: Confirmed the signing of Chiquinho Conde's new contract as national team coach, valid until 31 July 2027, saying the main objective set is to secure the Mambas' qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

a2325.speaker: Provincial executive of Tete
a2325.name: Provincial executive of Tete
a2325.speech: Intends to raise this year the level of rural water supply coverage from 54.12 percent to 56 percent, drilling 31 boreholes, rehabilitating another 50 and completing 15 supply systems.

a2348.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a2348.name: Seydou Asman
a2348.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a2348.speech: Thanked all the structures involved for their commitment to this process, welcoming their willingness to support the State in its mission of efficiently distributing cement, especially following the reduction in the price of this construction material decided by the President of the CNSP ; "This collaboration demonstrates the transporters' commitment to contributing actively to the development of our economy by ensuring efficient distribution throughout the national territory" ; stated that all parties had shown an unshakeable determination to bring the agreement to fruition, ensuring the continuity of cement supply ; "Since the implementation of the ordinance, the market has never lacked supply, even in the face of speculation. The tensions were due to strong demand, because after the signing, in less than two weeks, the cement plants managed to put more than 98,000 tonnes on the market", affirming that this protocol would strengthen distribution capacity for the benefit of all Nigeriens.

a2348.speaker: Gérard Delanne, representative of the Collectives of Goods Transporters' Unions of Niger
a2348.name: Gérard Delanne
a2348.title: representative of the Collectives of Goods Transporters' Unions of Niger
a2348.speech: Thanked the Nigerien authorities for this initiative which, he said, allows all parties to "speak the same language" ; "After long discussions, you have tackled our long-standing concerns head-on and today you are the architects of the future of the transport sector through the supervising ministry" ; reiterated the wish that this partnership be maintained and contribute to the sustainable development of the sector.

a2348.speaker: Memorandum of understanding signed between the Government of Niger and the goods transporters' unions (document)
a2348.name: Memorandum of understanding signed between the Government of Niger and the goods transporters' unions (document)
a2348.speech: It is agreed that the Collectives undertake to apply and scrupulously respect the transport prices per tonne of CEM II 32.5 cement by region as set by the Government (Niamey 8,000 F, Dosso 7,000, Tahoua 2,000 F, Maradi 8,000 F, Zinder 10,000 F, Diffa 12,000, Agadez 12,000 F and Tillabéri 10,000 F), while the Government undertakes to guarantee exclusively to Nigerien transporters the carriage of cement freight from production points to all regions of Niger; the protocol enters into force on the date of its signature.

a2369.speaker: Daniel (last name withheld), student and altar server at a church in Dessie
a2369.name: Daniel (last name withheld)
a2369.title: student and altar server at a church in Dessie
a2369.speech: "I withdrew all I had," said Daniel, declining to disclose how much he had in his account.

a2369.speaker: A source at the Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE) (anonymous)
a2369.name: A source at the Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE) (anonymous)
a2369.speech: "There are reports that some branches in Meqelle are open and handling small transactions," a source at the CBE told Fortune.

a2369.speaker: Aklilu Wubet, Acting President of Wegagen Bank
a2369.name: Aklilu Wubet
a2369.title: Acting President of Wegagen Bank
a2369.speech: Describes it as being challenging to navigate through these tough waters; disclosed that the Bank had lost about 2.3 billion Br in deposits as customers withdrew their savings. "Thankfully, we've regained our customers," he told Fortune.

a2369.speaker: Wegagen Bank (disclosure)
a2369.name: Wegagen Bank (disclosure)
a2369.speech: The Bank later disclosed the arms found in its branches were stored for security purposes, standard practice for all banks securing vaults.

a2369.speaker: Aklilu Wubet, Acting President of Wegagen Bank
a2369.name: Aklilu Wubet
a2369.title: Acting President of Wegagen Bank
a2369.speech: Applauded the central bank for having gone the extra mile to help the Bank stay afloat in the troubled waters. "It was beyond my expectations," said Aklilu.

a2369.speaker: Abdulmenan Mohammed, finance expert based in London
a2369.name: Abdulmenan Mohammed
a2369.title: finance expert based in London
a2369.speech: Says mobilising one billion Birr by Wegagen shows a not-so-impressive performance. "It significantly affects the Bank's lending capacity," he told Fortune.

a2369.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia survey
a2369.name: National Bank of Ethiopia survey
a2369.speech: A survey conducted before federal forces left Tigray Regional State at the end of June identified that many branches had been completely damaged while others were looted.

a2369.speaker: Solomon Desta, vice governor of financial institutions at the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a2369.name: Solomon Desta
a2369.title: vice governor of financial institutions at the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a2369.speech: "A little over half of the branches in the region were operational until banks and the regulator lost all control and communications," Solomon Desta told Fortune. "We discussed how to support severely affected banks and intervened to allow them to cash out their NBE bonds." ; According to the Vice Governor, banks can benefit from the conversion of maturing bonds to treasury bills.

a2369.speaker: Federal authorities and city officials
a2369.name: Federal authorities and city officials
a2369.speech: Convinced that there is an active and coordinated "economic sabotage," they have taken a series of measures, including the arbitrary closure of businesses and suspensions of asset transfers.

a2369.speaker: Government officials
a2369.name: Government officials
a2369.speech: Attributed the move forbidding banks to provide collateralised loans to a massive increase in outstanding credit to the private sector.

a2369.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia (central bank)
a2369.name: National Bank of Ethiopia (central bank)
a2369.speech: Asserted the heavy loan disbursement was to be blamed for a significant uptake in "capital flight," which was subsequently exhibited in dollarisation, pushing the parallel market value of the Dollar to an all-time high of over 70 Br.

a2369.speaker: Banks (industry)
a2369.name: Banks (industry)
a2369.speech: Exasperated by the increase of reserve requirements the central bank issued last month, banks have reported their liquidity status is "below adequate."

a2369.speaker: Officials of the central bank
a2369.name: Officials of the central bank
a2369.speech: Remain adamant that they have met their goals in weakening the parallel market with these restrictions.

a2369.speaker: Solomon Desta, vice governor of financial institutions at the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a2369.name: Solomon Desta
a2369.title: vice governor of financial institutions at the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a2369.speech: "These restrictions will not be here forever," Solomon said. "They'll be lifted as the conflict ends, and those sabotaging the economy can no longer cause harm."

a2369.speaker: Mekonnen Yelemwessen, Chief Executive Officer of Amhara Credit & Savings Institute (ACSI)
a2369.name: Mekonnen Yelemwessen
a2369.title: Chief Executive Officer of Amhara Credit & Savings Institute (ACSI)
a2369.speech: Estimates the Institute will require one billion Birr to recover its branches and rebuild damaged assets. "We'll seek support from the government and other sources," said Mekonnen.

a2369.speaker: Industry insiders
a2369.name: Industry insiders
a2369.speech: Caution there should be a coordinated national effort to conduct assessments, determine the damages and how to report them on annual financial statements for shareholders and regulators.

a2369.speaker: Zafu Eyesuswork, industry veteran
a2369.name: Zafu Eyesuswork
a2369.title: industry veteran
a2369.speech: Observes the conflict has taken an undeniable toll on the financial sector; acknowledges that some financial institutions have been hit harder than others, making it difficult to prescribe any remedies for the situation; urges that the focus should be attaining a satisfactory degree of separation between politics and business.

a2369.speaker: UN-OCHA
a2369.name: UN-OCHA
a2369.speech: According to the UN-OCHA, the amount of cash allowed to be brought by humanitarian organisations into the region is still limited and insufficient to sustain humanitarian operations.

a2369.speaker: Humanitarian organisations
a2369.name: Humanitarian organisations
a2369.speech: Estimated 6.5 million dollars are needed every week.

a2369.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) report, published August 2021
a2369.name: World Food Programme (WFP) report
a2369.title: published August 2021
a2369.speech: "Challenges in accessing cash and fuel hampered the humanitarian response," states the report. "Consequently, only 40pc of the planned beneficiaries received assistance."

a2380.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.name: Mokhethi Shelile
a2380.title: Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.speech: Revealed, in a media briefing following the announcement, that this development comes as Lesotho was in the process of negotiating the extension of its African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) benefits.

a2380.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.name: Mokhethi Shelile
a2380.title: Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.speech: Explained that Lesotho primarily exports three main products to the US - trout, apparel and car seats. “These industries are vital to the country’s economy, with approximately 11 industrial firms exporting to the US and employing around 12 000 workers, most of whom are women, particularly in the Ha Thetsane Industrial Area,” he said, adding that with the new tariffs in place, there is growing concern that jobs might be at risk ; He emphasized the urgency of engaging in discussions with US trade executives to address the issue.

a2380.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.name: Mokhethi Shelile
a2380.title: Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.speech: Said initially a 10 percent baseline tariff was introduced, reflecting trade performance between the two countries, and then an additional 40 percent was applied, bringing the total tariff to 50 percent ; said the 99 percent trade deficit represents the trade imbalance between Lesotho and the US, with Lesotho exporting goods worth approximately USD 240 million to the US whereas the US exports only $3 million to Lesotho, just one percent of the trade volume ; “This vast difference led to the US imposing a reciprocal tariff of 50 percent,” he said, adding that Lesotho needs to act swiftly and hold meetings with US executives about this matter, while also strengthening the relationship between the two countries.

a2380.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.name: Mokhethi Shelile
a2380.title: Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.speech: Stressed the importance of diversifying Lesotho’s export markets beyond the US: “We should not rely solely on the US market.” He pointed out that South Africa exports globally and that Lesotho should focus more on domestic and regional trade within the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), where South Africa plans to source 80 percent of its goods locally, thus Lesotho to take advantage of that ; “Over the past months, around 10 firms have reopened or expanded their operations, but only one of these firms exports to the US. As a result, the tariff increase could disproportionately affect businesses reliant on American markets,” he said.

a2380.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.name: Mokhethi Shelile
