a2380.title: Lesotho Minister of Trade, Industry and Business Development
a2380.speech: Said goods already in transit to the US will not be affected by the new tariffs, but those still in production could face severe consequences. “Starting from today, the expectation was that industrial workers will begin losing their jobs. However, we have taken steps to ensure they continue working while we address the issue,” Shelile reassured.

a2380.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations
a2380.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a2380.title: Lesotho Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations
a2380.speech: Emphasized, during the same press conference, that the country still maintains strong relations with the US: “The 99 percent figure reflects a trade deficit, not a breakdown in relations. The US is simply prioritizing its own economic interests,” the minister said.

a2433.speaker: United States and Saudi Arabia (joint statement)
a2433.name: United States and Saudi Arabia (joint statement)
a2433.speech: “The facilitators share the frustration of the Sudanese people about the uneven implementation of previous ceasefires. The facilitators proposed this latest initiative in an effort to break the cycle of violence. Should the parties fail to observe the 24-hour ceasefire, facilitators will be compelled to consider adjourning the Jeddah talks.” ; emphasised the importance of the mini truce: “If observed, the 24-hour ceasefire will provide an important opportunity to deliver humanitarian assistance and for the parties to undertake confidence-building measures that could permit the resumption of the Jeddah talks.”

a2433.speaker: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)
a2433.name: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)
a2433.speech: On 31 May, suspended its participation in the Jeddah talks, accusing the RSF of lacking commitment through violations of ceasefire agreements.

a2433.speaker: Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti), leader of the Rapid Support Forces
a2433.name: Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti)
a2433.title: leader of the Rapid Support Forces
a2433.speech: In an interview with News24, blamed the SAF of the same (violations of ceasefire agreements).

a2433.speaker: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) statement
a2433.name: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) statement
a2433.speech: Said it took the facilitators’ efforts seriously: “The RSF appreciates the tremendous contribution of the United States and Saudi Arabia in helping to find a path to end this war.”

a2728.speaker: Health stakeholders in Tanzania
a2728.name: Health stakeholders in Tanzania
a2728.speech: Described the contribution of Dr Daimond Simbeye, who was a public health expert, especially in voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC), which contributes to reducing HIV infections by 60 percent.

a2728.speaker: George Mgomella, Director of Projects, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Tanzania, US Embassy
a2728.name: George Mgomella
a2728.title: Director of Projects, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Tanzania, US Embassy
a2728.speech: Speaking at the funeral held on 13 September 2024, said the death of Dr Simbeye is a blow to the nation because of the contribution he made in controlling HIV infections ; said Dr Simbeye had served CDC for 12 years, during which he took part in controlling those infections by running the voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) campaign ; “His leadership and his expertise were important in helping Tanzania’s VMMC efforts to reach and exceed targets on time, and also to improve the quality of services in community settings” ; said that in the campaign some 800,000 to 900,000 young people reaching the age of 15 were reached with the service every year ; “Simbeye was overseeing funds from the US President’s fund (PEPFAR) to enable that group of young people to be circumcised free of charge in Tanzania.”

a2728.speaker: Susan Mmbando, Circumcision Coordinator, Ministry of Health (Tanzania)
a2728.name: Susan Mmbando
a2728.title: Circumcision Coordinator, Ministry of Health (Tanzania)
a2728.speech: Said that in the campaign the deceased enabled more than six million men to be circumcised in 17 regions of the country ; said she had known Dr Simbeye for 25 years, as a public servant and later as a CDC employee ; “I worked with him while he was at CDC on male circumcision matters, so his contribution to the government is supervising seven model regions in circumcision, which are Shinyanga, Mwanza, Geita, Simiyu, Mara, Kigoma and Kagera, among the 17 priority regions.” “The last time we were with the late Dr Simbeye was in Morogoro region from 2 to 6 September 2024, drawing up a sustainable circumcision plan, and he made many contributions to that guideline.”

a2790.speaker: IMF spokesperson (via Ethiopia's Fana Broadcasting Corporate)
a2790.name: IMF spokesperson (via Ethiopia's Fana Broadcasting Corporate)
a2790.speech: Said they were doing technical work to prepare for a potential IMF-supported programme.

a2790.speaker: Alvaro Piris, leader of the IMF mission visit to Ethiopia
a2790.name: Alvaro Piris
a2790.title: leader of the IMF mission visit to Ethiopia
a2790.speech: Said in a statement: "We made progress in discussing the scope for IMF support for this reform programme." ; "The IMF team welcomes the authorities' Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda (HGER II), an ambitious reform program that aims to address key macroeconomic vulnerabilities and unleash Ethiopia's considerable economic potential. Discussions will continue in Washington, DC, next week, in the context of the IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings, and in coming weeks."

a2790.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2790.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2790.speech: In late March, the IMF said it welcomed the progress Ethiopia had made in restoring lasting peace and stability following an agreement in November to cease hostilities, including by the restoration of humanitarian assistance and basic services to the northern Ethiopia.

a2878.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2878.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2878.speech: Reported that a four-year-old child had become the second person to die of Ebola in Uganda since the outbreak announced at the end of January.

a2878.speaker: Ugandan health authorities
a2878.name: Ugandan health authorities
a2878.speech: Confirmed last Tuesday that the country had recorded 10 infections with the Sudan strain of the virus.

a3148.speaker: Donald Trump, former U.S. President and Republican presidential candidate
a3148.name: Donald Trump
a3148.title: former U.S. President and Republican presidential candidate
a3148.speech: The false claims [about the hurricane response] are being fuelled by former president and Republican candidate Donald Trump and others, shortly before the presidential elections.

a3148.speaker: White House (statement)
a3148.name: White House (statement)
a3148.speech: According to the White House statement, about $911 million was allocated to the damage caused by Hurricane Helene, while about $620 million was allocated to recovery from Hurricane Milton; other funds were allocated to measures such as assistance to agriculture, going to six states: Florida, South Carolina, Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia.

a3148.speaker: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA)
a3148.name: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA)
a3148.speech: Disclosed that it had run out of money for the disaster assistance loans it offers to small businesses, homeowners and renters ; said it had so far awarded $48 million in loans to survivors of the two hurricanes.

a3148.speaker: Deanne Criswell, FEMA Administrator
a3148.name: Deanne Criswell
a3148.title: FEMA Administrator
a3148.speech: Has repeatedly said that her agency has enough money in its humanitarian relief fund to respond to Helene and Milton ; but stressed that the agency will eventually need supplementary funding from Congress, and that if that does not happen FEMA will resort to so-called “immediate needs funding,” meaning it would stop paying for previous disasters and save its money for life-saving missions during any new incidents.

a3192.speaker: Eswatini procurement rules
a3192.name: Eswatini procurement rules
a3192.speech: State that tenders should go to emaSwati unless there is a clear and proven need for specialist knowledge or skills that are not locally available.

a3192.speaker: Kenya's procurement laws
a3192.name: Kenya's procurement laws
a3192.speech: State that at least 40 per cent of government contracts must be awarded to local companies and youth-owned businesses.

a3192.speaker: Botswana government business policies
a3192.name: Botswana government business policies
a3192.speech: Clearly state that most of the diamonds must benefit citizens and locals get a share in any profits made from exports.

a3196.speaker: The Vatican
a3196.name: The Vatican
a3196.speech: Says Pope Francis, the first Latin American pontiff in the history of the Roman Catholic Church, has died aged 88.

a3196.speaker: Giorgia Meloni, Italian Prime Minister
a3196.name: Giorgia Meloni
a3196.title: Italian Prime Minister
a3196.speech: Mourned the loss of “a great man, a great shepherd” and expressed deep sorrow: “I had the privilege of enjoying his friendship, his advice, his teachings, which never ceased, not even during times of trial and suffering” ; “We say goodbye to the holy father with a heart full of sadness.”

a3196.speaker: Argentine presidency office
a3196.name: Argentine presidency office
a3196.speech: Said that it deeply “regretted” the death of the first Argentine leader of the Catholic Church.

a3196.speaker: Javier Milei, President of Argentina
a3196.name: Javier Milei
a3196.title: President of Argentina
a3196.speech: Praised Francis' focus on inter-religious dialogue, encouragement of spirituality amongst the young, and focus on cost-cutting in the Vatican.

a3196.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission President
a3196.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a3196.title: European Commission President
a3196.speech: Said Francis's life was defined by his efforts to build a fairer and more peaceful world: “He inspired millions, far beyond the Catholic Church, with his humility and love so pure for the less fortunate.”

a3196.speaker: The White House (social media post)
a3196.name: The White House (social media post)
a3196.speech: Shared a tribute on social media, writing “Rest in Peace, Pope Francis” alongside a photo of the pope meeting President Donald Trump and the first lady.

a3196.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (Truth Social post)
a3196.name: Donald Trump
a3196.title: US President (Truth Social post)
a3196.speech: “Rest in Peace Pope Francis! May God Bless him and all who loved him!”

a3196.speaker: JD Vance, US Vice President
a3196.name: JD Vance
a3196.title: US Vice President
a3196.speech: “My heart goes out to the millions of Christians all over the world who loved him.”

a3196.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a3196.name: Vladimir Putin
a3196.title: Russian President
a3196.speech: Expressed his “sincere condolences,” praising the efforts of Francis to strengthen ties between the Russian Orthodox and Catholic Churches.

a3196.speaker: The Moscow Patriarchate
a3196.name: The Moscow Patriarchate
a3196.speech: Echoed the sentiment, saying the late pontiff had played a key role in advancing dialogue between the two branches of Christianity.

a3196.speaker: Narendra Modi, Indian Prime Minister
a3196.name: Narendra Modi
a3196.title: Indian Prime Minister
a3196.speech: “Pope Francis will always be remembered as a beacon of compassion, humility and spiritual courage by millions across the world. He diligently served the poor and downtrodden. For those who were suffering, he ignited a spirit of hope.”

a3196.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a3196.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3196.title: French President
a3196.speech: Praised the pontiff for his enduring solidarity with society's most vulnerable: “In this time of war and brutality, he had a sense for the other, for the most fragile,” commending his humility.

a3196.speaker: Ferdinand Marcos Jr, President of the Philippines
a3196.name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr
a3196.title: President of the Philippines
a3196.speech: Called Francis “the best pope in my lifetime,” praising his humility, faith, and compassion for the poor.

a3196.speaker: Cardinal Pablo Virgilio David
a3196.name: Cardinal Pablo Virgilio David
a3196.speech: Expressed shock and urged churches to ring their bells and call people to prayer for the pope's “eternal repose”.

a3196.speaker: Andrzej Duda, Polish President
a3196.name: Andrzej Duda
a3196.title: Polish President
a3196.speech: Hailed Francis as “a great apostle of mercy”, saying the pontiff's example offered answers to contemporary challenges: “In his pastoral ministry, he was guided by humility and simplicity.”

a3196.speaker: Felix Bolanos, Spanish Justice Minister
a3196.name: Felix Bolanos
a3196.title: Spanish Justice Minister
a3196.speech: Said in a televised address that the country regrets “the death of a good man and a great pope,” and praised Francis's “reformist” papacy that “will leave a legacy for history”.

a3196.speaker: Anthony Albanese, Australian Prime Minister
a3196.name: Anthony Albanese
a3196.title: Australian Prime Minister
a3196.speech: Said Francis would be mourned by Australians of all faiths, describing him as “a devoted champion and loving father” to Catholics: “His compassion embraced all humanity” ; “He urged us to hear the cry of the earth and remember all we share.”

a3196.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopian Prime Minister
a3196.name: Abiy Ahmed
a3196.title: Ethiopian Prime Minister
a3196.speech: Said the pope's passing was a loss not only for Catholics but for humanity: “May his soul rest in eternal peace, and may his legacy of compassion, humility and service to humanity continue to inspire generations to come.”

a3196.speaker: Jose Ramos-Horta, President of Timor-Leste
a3196.name: Jose Ramos-Horta
a3196.title: President of Timor-Leste
a3196.speech: Described Francis's death as a global loss and announced the nation's flags would be lowered to half-staff for a week with a Mass to follow in tribute to the pope's life and service.

a3196.speaker: Friedrich Merz, Germany's chancellor-in-waiting (post on X)
a3196.name: Friedrich Merz
a3196.title: Germany's chancellor-in-waiting (post on X)
a3196.speech: Said Francis would be remembered for his unwavering commitment to the marginalised: “He was guided by humility and faith in God's mercy.”

a3196.speaker: Esmail Baghaei, spokesman for Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3196.name: Esmail Baghaei
a3196.title: spokesman for Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3196.speech: Acknowledged Francis's global spiritual influence, saying Iran “extends condolences to all Christians around the world.”

a3196.speaker: The Dalai Lama (statement)
a3196.name: The Dalai Lama (statement)
a3196.speech: Offered Buddhist prayers and wrote to the papal envoy to “express his sadness” over the death: “Pope Francis dedicated himself to the service of others… consistently revealing by his own actions how to live a simple, but meaningful life” ; “The best tribute we can pay to him is to be a warm-hearted person, serving others wherever and in whatever way we can”.

a3196.speaker: King Charles
a3196.name: King Charles
a3196.speech: Said he was “most deeply saddened,” praising Pope Francis' “compassion,” commitment to unity, and the environment.

a3196.speaker: Keir Starmer, British Prime Minister
a3196.name: Keir Starmer
a3196.title: British Prime Minister
a3196.speech: Expressed his condolences, saying Francis's “tireless efforts to promote a world that is fairer for all” would be remembered.

a3196.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General (statement)
a3196.name: Antonio Guterres
a3196.title: UN Secretary-General (statement)
a3196.speech: Hailed what he called Pope Francis' historic influence as a voice for peace and human dignity: “I join the world in mourning the passing of His Holiness Pope Francis, a messenger of hope, humility and humanity.”

a3656.speaker: General Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a3656.name: General Assimi Goita
a3656.title: President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a3656.speech: Prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died, offered his condolences to their families and expressed wishes for a prompt recovery to the injured, following the tragedies that occurred at the gold-panning sites at Kokoyo (Kangaba District) and Bilalikoto (Kenieba District) ; instructed the Government to strengthen measures to avoid human and environmental tragedies in the country ; further instructed the repeal of the appointment orders of the administrative officials directly involved in the incidents, the revision of certain legal texts, the suspension of artisanal mining permits granted to foreign nationals, and the launch of the dissolution procedure of the Municipal Council of Dabia.

a3656.speaker: General Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a3656.name: General Assimi Goita
a3656.title: President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a3656.speech: Called on the population to strictly respect the measures for prevention of and fight against dengue.

a3656.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a3656.name: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a3656.speech: Reported on the draft texts relating to the ratification of the Budget Support Agreement including a loan, signed in Bamako on 26 February 2025, between the Government of the Republic of Mali and the Qatar Fund for Development, under which the Fund grants Mali budget support of 50 million US dollars.

a3656.speaker: Minister of Economy and Finance of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a3656.name: Minister of Economy and Finance of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a3656.speech: Reported on a draft ordinance amending Law No. 06-067 of 29 December 2006 establishing the General Tax Code, in order to adapt it to the new Mining Code.

a3656.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a3656.name: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a3656.speech: Reported on three draft decrees on the Universal Health Insurance Scheme: on the deadlines and procedures for concluding agreements between the National Health Insurance Fund and health care providers, on the standard management-delegation agreements, and on the principles of preferential pricing and coverage rates for health care services.

a3656.speaker: Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals of Mali
a3656.name: Minister of Justice and Human Rights
a3656.title: Keeper of the Seals of Mali
a3656.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of Mali's participation in the "High-Level Segment" on the human rights situation held from 24 to 26 February 2025 in Geneva, and said Mali conveyed strong messages, notably the reaffirmation of the Government's determination to implement all recommendations accepted during the Universal Periodic Review, the remarkable improvement in the overall security situation, the pooling of defense means by the Heads of State of the Alliance of Sahel States, the determination to fight impunity, and the reiteration of the appeal to the international community to avoid the politicization and instrumentalization of human rights.

a3656.speaker: Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research of Mali
a3656.name: Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research of Mali
a3656.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his mission to Timbuktu from 25 to 27 February 2025 on the operationalization of the University of Timbuktu, noting with interest and satisfaction the evolution of the process.

a3656.speaker: Minister of Youth and Sports, in charge of Civic Instruction and Citizen Building of Mali
a3656.name: Minister of Youth and Sports
a3656.title: in charge of Civic Instruction and Citizen Building of Mali
a3656.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the meetings intended for students called "Citizen Masterclass," a mission of civic education and patriotic engagement to make students "model and responsible citizens."

a3656.speaker: Minister of Agriculture of Mali
a3656.name: Minister of Agriculture of Mali
a3656.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his participation in the 19th edition of the National Cereals Exchange, which recorded the signing of 61 contracts for a total of 1 billion 184 million 410 thousand CFA francs.

a3656.speaker: Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training of Mali
a3656.name: Minister of National Entrepreneurship
a3656.title: Employment and Vocational Training of Mali
a3656.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the launch of the recruitment of 2,500 new interns for the 14th contingent of the vocational training internship program, with 15,021 files registered, and of his field mission to the Gao Region from 27 February to 1 March 2025.

a3656.speaker: Minister of Industry and Commerce of Mali
a3656.name: Minister of Industry and Commerce of Mali
a3656.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the holding in Mali of the 1st edition of the Africa Investment Forum of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, on the theme "Unlocking Africa's Investment Potential."

a3656.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a3656.name: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a3656.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the epidemiological situation of the country, marked by an increase in the number of confirmed dengue cases compared with the past week.

a3694.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (message read by his advisor Andre Azoulay)
a3694.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (message read by his advisor Andre Azoulay)
a3694.speech: In his address, advocated for a fundamental overhaul of global financial governance to ensure equitable representation for Africa and establish fairer financing conditions, emphasizing a spirit of solidarity and South-South cooperation ; commended the Mo Ibrahim Foundation’s efforts in fostering critical dialogue on the continent’s development; however, he underscored that current international crises are exacerbating inequalities between nations and impeding progress towards the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, and stressed Africa’s urgent need to transform these formidable challenges into tangible opportunities.

a3694.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (message read by his advisor Andre Azoulay)
a3694.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (message read by his advisor Andre Azoulay)
a3694.speech: Outlined four strategic guidelines crucial for harmonious and prosperous African growth: a paradigm shift in development financing, advocating for greater mobilization of domestic resources and the creation of innovative financing mechanisms that reduce reliance on debt-generating foreign aid; establishing an institutional, economic, and social environment more conducive to attracting investment and generating employment, emphasizing good governance, transparency, investor protection, and a resolute fight against corruption; strengthening trade flows within the continent, noting that intra-African trade currently accounts for only 16 percent of total trade, significantly less than Europe’s 60 percent, and welcoming the launch of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA); and the strategic development of Africa’s abundant natural resources, urging African countries to process this wealth locally to generate added value, create jobs, and bolster regional integration.

a3694.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (message read by his advisor Andre Azoulay)
a3694.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (message read by his advisor Andre Azoulay)
a3694.speech: Reiterated that Morocco, leveraging its extensive expertise in renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, and infrastructure, is actively serving as a catalyst for South-South partnerships, citing key projects including the African Atlantic Gas Pipeline (AAGP) and the Atlantic Initiative, and highlighted innovative financing mechanisms developed by Morocco such as the Mohammed VI Investment Fund and the Casablanca Finance City platform ; concluded his message by urging the international community to prioritize financing for African development, particularly in anticipation of the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development scheduled to be held in Seville, and called for a comprehensive reform of the global financial architecture that fully incorporates African realities and ensures enhanced representation for the continent’s countries in international bodies ; “Development cannot be decreed; it is built through ambitious policies, investment in human capital, and rigorous economic governance.”

a3708.speaker: Selibe Mochoboroane, Minister of Health of Lesotho (statement released in Maseru)
a3708.name: Selibe Mochoboroane
a3708.title: Minister of Health of Lesotho (statement released in Maseru)
a3708.speech: Declared he will revoke licenses held by operators failing to comply with legislation, invoking Section 23 of the Drugs of Abuse Act of 2008 – as amended: “The Ministry of Health reminds all cannabis operators that licenses are valid for 12 months and must be renewed each year, as required by the Drugs of Abuse Act of 2008” ; “Previously, the Ministry requested all license to report on the operational status of their businesses. This was a legal requirement…” ; stated that compliance with the laws and regulations governing the cultivation, processing, and export of medicinal cannabis is not optional, and those who fail to meet the required standards, including operational and ethical benchmarks, will face cancellation of their licenses ; declared that licenses not reported to the ministry are considered cancelled and those not renewed within 12 months are similarly considered cancelled, adding that “cancelled licences will not be renewed. Operators must reapply as new applicants if they wish to continue operating” ; stated licensees would, within the given 12 months, have to demonstrate adherence to requirements covering security, cultivation standards, processing facilities and financial reporting, and did not directly address the specific corruption allegations during his announcement, focusing instead on future compliance and on government's commitment to a “clean, well-regulated, and beneficial” cannabis industry.

a3708.speaker: Multiple sources within the cannabis industry (anonymous, speaking for fear of reprisal)
a3708.name: Multiple sources within the cannabis industry (anonymous
a3708.title: speaking for fear of reprisal)
a3708.speech: Allege a pattern of irregularities such as bribery for licenses – with claims that significant bribes were paid to officials within the Ministry of Health and other relevant bodies to secure cultivation and processing licenses, suggesting a ‘pay-to-play’ system favouring well-connected individuals or foreign investors over potentially qualified local entities ; allegations that some licenses were issued to entities with no demonstrable capacity or intent to cultivate, possibly acting as fronts or holding assets for speculative resale at inflated prices, and that proper vetting processes for financial backing, technical expertise and adherence to security protocols were bypassed for certain applicants.

a3708.speaker: Industry consultant who has worked with multiple license applicants (anonymous)
a3708.name: Industry consultant who has worked with multiple license applicants (anonymous)
a3708.speech: “These aren't just rumours” ; “There's a palpable sense that the playing field wasn't level. Certain applications seemed to magically jump the queue or overcome hurdles that stalled others, fuelling suspicion about under-the-table dealings.”

a3708.speaker: Industry insider based in Maseru (anonymous)
a3708.name: Industry insider based in Maseru (anonymous)
a3708.speech: “The minister's statement is a necessary step, but it's reactive. The damage to investor confidence might already be significant. Cancelling non-compliant licenses is crucial for integrity, but the government must simultaneously demonstrate a thorough, transparent investigation into how those licenses were issued in the first place. Sweeping this under the rug will only prolong the crisis.”

a3708.speaker: Another industry player (anonymous)
a3708.name: Another industry player (anonymous)
a3708.speech: “The minister is wielding a big stick, and rightly so on compliance, but the elephant in the room is the original sin – how did allegedly unqualified or corrupt entities get licenses? Until there is accountability for that, and a demonstrably transparent process moving forward, the sector's reputation will remain tarnished.”

a3812.speaker: Los Angeles jury (verdict)
a3812.name: Los Angeles jury (verdict)
a3812.speech: ordered Johnson & Johnson to pay $966 million to the family of a woman who died from mesothelioma, finding the company liable; the jury ordered J&J to pay $16 million in compensatory damages and $950 million in punitive damages.

a3812.speaker: Court filings
a3812.name: Court filings
a3812.speech: According to court filings, the jury ordered the damages award, and J&J is facing lawsuits from more than 67,000 plaintiffs who say they were diagnosed with cancer after using baby powder and other talc products.

a3812.speaker: U.S. Supreme Court
a3812.name: U.S. Supreme Court
a3812.speech: has found that punitive damages should generally be no more than nine times compensatory damages.

a3812.speaker: Erik Haas, Johnson & Johnson’s worldwide vice president of litigation
a3812.name: Erik Haas
a3812.title: Johnson & Johnson’s worldwide vice president of litigation
a3812.speech: said in a statement that the company plans to immediately appeal, calling the verdict “egregious and unconstitutional” ; “The plaintiff lawyers in this Moore case based their arguments on ‘junk science’ that never should have been presented to the jury.”

a3812.speaker: Johnson & Johnson (company)
a3812.name: Johnson & Johnson (company)
a3812.speech: has said its products are safe, do not contain asbestos, and do not cause cancer.

a3812.speaker: Trey Branham, one of the attorneys representing Moore’s family
a3812.name: Trey Branham
a3812.title: one of the attorneys representing Moore’s family
a3812.speech: said after the verdict that his team is “hopeful that Johnson & Johnson will finally accept responsibility for these senseless deaths.”

a3821.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a3821.name: Vladimir Putin
a3821.title: Russian President
a3821.speech: In his address, reiterated that the time to define a sovereign and context-specific economic development path is now, citing the BRICS bloc’s growth from representing 20% to 40% of global GDP for over two decades, and emphasized restructuring investment climates, reducing bureaucratic burdens, and embracing technological advancement as core to building resilient, self-determined economies.

a3821.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a3821.name: Vladimir Putin
a3821.title: Russian President
a3821.speech: Remarks underscored Russia’s focus on fiscal discipline, highlighting the importance of maintaining budget surpluses, creating sovereign funds, and engaging in long-term economic planning as shock absorbers in times of uncertainty.

a3821.speaker: SPIEF 2025 forum (concluding assertion)
a3821.name: SPIEF 2025 forum (concluding assertion)
a3821.speech: Concluded with an ambitious assertion: the world is undergoing profound economic, political, and institutional shifts, and it is imperative that all governments, and especially those in Africa, rethink and reorganize their strategies to better position themselves within the evolving global financial ecosystem.

a3821.speaker: Eye Radio (editor’s note)
a3821.name: Eye Radio (editor’s note)
a3821.speech: Editor’s Note: ‘The views expressed in the above articles, as published by Eye Radio, are entirely those of the writer. Any claims made are the responsibility of the author, not Eye Radio’s.’

a4234.speaker: Yonis Ali Guedi, Djiboutian Minister of Energy, in charge of Natural Resources
a4234.name: Yonis Ali Guedi
a4234.title: Djiboutian Minister of Energy, in charge of Natural Resources
a4234.speech: Emphasised from the outset the quality of the multidimensional links of friendship and cooperation between the United States and the Republic of Djibouti; reaffirmed the wish of the Government of Djibouti to attract American investment in the energy sector in order to carry out structuring energy projects within the framework of a win-win partnership.

a4234.speaker: Yonis Ali Guedi, Djiboutian Minister of Energy, in charge of Natural Resources
a4234.name: Yonis Ali Guedi
a4234.title: Djiboutian Minister of Energy, in charge of Natural Resources
a4234.speech: Presented to the new American ambassador the ins and outs of the national energy policy implemented in Djibouti (the priority energy projects, the objectives pursued, the challenges to be met, notably the necessary acceleration of access to energy for urban and rural populations, the role of private investment in the energy sector and future prospects); insisted on the need to replicate the solar electricity charging station project initiated at Kalaf, in the Tadjourah region, in the other regions of the country so as to allow local communities to benefit from it.

a4234.speaker: Cynthia Kierscht, new Ambassador of the United States of America to Djibouti
a4234.name: Cynthia Kierscht
a4234.title: new Ambassador of the United States of America to Djibouti
a4234.speech: Thanked the Minister for the warm welcome and enquired about the issues linked to the various energy projects driven forward in Djibouti, the challenges to be overcome and the priority projects to be carried out.

a4234.speaker: Cynthia Kierscht, new Ambassador of the United States of America to Djibouti
a4234.name: Cynthia Kierscht
a4234.title: new Ambassador of the United States of America to Djibouti
a4234.speech: Indicated that her priority consisted in attracting American investors into Djibouti’s energy sector; informed the Minister of the forthcoming mission of officials of the American company CREC, interested in the project for electricity production from biomass; committed herself to accompanying the Ministry of Energy in the realisation of the various projects under way; and saluted the enlightened vision pursued and the imperative necessity of implementing the projects undertaken.

a4278.speaker: National Drought Management Authority (NDMA), Kenya
a4278.name: National Drought Management Authority (NDMA)
a4278.title: Kenya
a4278.speech: Said Monday that at least a million people in Kenya are struggling with food insecurity and in need of humanitarian assistance ; noted in a report released in Nairobi that the affected people are in 23 out of the country's 47 counties, which are classified as arid and semi-arid ; revealed that households sold their harvests to cover other costs, often at the expense of maintaining healthy eating and chronic challenges associated with stunting.

a4278.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) report
a4278.name: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) report
a4278.speech: Noted in July that the number of food-insecure people in the Horn of Africa stood at 66.7 million, among them 39.1 million from six of the eight IGAD member states, namely Djibouti, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

a4328.speaker: Source cited for the Israeli decision (unnamed)
a4328.name: Source cited for the Israeli decision (unnamed)
a4328.speech: According to the same source, the decision was approved due to a request from the President of the United States, Joe Biden, who was visiting Israel.

a4328.speaker: Israeli government (official statement)
a4328.name: Israeli government (official statement)
a4328.speech: In a communiqué, the Israeli executive indicated that it “will not impede” the supply of food, water and medicines, provided that these goods do not reach the Palestinian Islamist movement Hamas; the note does not mention fuel, which is running short.

a4328.speaker: Israel (government position)
a4328.name: Israel (government position)
a4328.speech: Says it will not allow humanitarian aid to be routed through its territory to the Palestinian enclave, which has been controlled by Hamas since 2007; the Israeli Government also demanded that the International Red Cross be authorised to visit the Israelis held hostage in Gaza.

a4328.speaker: Egypt (government)
a4328.name: Egypt (government)
a4328.speech: Says the Rafah crossing, which has limited capacity, was damaged by Israeli air strikes.

a4429.speaker: Politico (citing sources)
a4429.name: Politico (citing sources)
a4429.speech: Reported, citing sources, that the US Department of Defense has decided to withdraw all American troops – 1,000 people – from Niger over the coming months.

a4429.speaker: United States (official announcement)
a4429.name: United States (official announcement)
a4429.speech: In April, the United States announced that it would begin discussing plans for an “orderly and responsible withdrawal” after the Nigerien authorities announced they would cancel the military cooperation agreement with Washington.

a4429.speaker: U.S. officials
a4429.name: U.S. officials
a4429.speech: Continued their consultations with the African country on the terms of the withdrawal, discussing the possibility that a portion of the American troops could remain on the state’s territory.

a4440.speaker: Melia Ismael Soumah, councillor, Committee on Planning, Financial Affairs and Budgetary Control of the National Transition Council (CNT)
a4440.name: Melia Ismael Soumah
a4440.title: councillor, Committee on Planning, Financial Affairs and Budgetary Control of the National Transition Council (CNT)
a4440.speech: Presented the report, saying that the government of the Republic of Guinea requested and obtained on 22 July 2024 from the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) financing of US$35,375,000 for the project to build 150 water boreholes equipped with hand pumps and 100 drinking-water supply systems in Upper Guinea and Forest Guinea ; She stated that this financing aims to improve the living conditions of populations in rural and peri-urban areas through access to drinking water and a public latrine service.

a4440.speaker: Melia Ismael Soumah, councillor, Committee on Planning, Financial Affairs and Budgetary Control of the National Transition Council (CNT)
a4440.name: Melia Ismael Soumah
a4440.title: councillor, Committee on Planning, Financial Affairs and Budgetary Control of the National Transition Council (CNT)
a4440.speech: "The terms and conditions attached to this loan agreement are as follows: the loan repayment period is 20 years, after a grace period of 5 years on amortization, beginning on the date immediately following the end of the grace period," she stressed ; She recalled that during this period the commissions and interest are payable: "The interest rate on the loan is 2.80% per year, payable every six months; the arrangement fee is payable at signature on the maximum loan amount at a rate of 1%; the commitment fee is 0.5% per year on the undisbursed amount; the special commitment fee is payable by the borrower on the amount of the letter of credit per indivisible quarter and set at a rate of 0.15%; the closing date for disbursements is set at 30 June 2028."

a4440.speaker: Melia Ismael Soumah, councillor, Committee on Planning, Financial Affairs and Budgetary Control of the National Transition Council (CNT)
a4440.name: Melia Ismael Soumah
a4440.title: councillor, Committee on Planning, Financial Affairs and Budgetary Control of the National Transition Council (CNT)
a4440.speech: Indicated that the goods, services and works financed by EBID will be carried out using the resources of the Indian line of credit: "These conditions require that 75% of the goods and services come solely from India," she insisted.

a4462.speaker: United States government, through the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID)
a4462.name: United States government
a4462.title: through the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID)
a4462.speech: Declared its latest strategic partnership with Ascend Studios, a creative-industry organization providing capacity building, mentorship, social, educational, and economic empowerment to women and youth, to propel Nigeria’s creative sector.

a4462.speaker: Melissa Jones, USAID Nigeria Mission Director
a4462.name: Melissa Jones
a4462.title: USAID Nigeria Mission Director
a4462.speech: Remarked, “The U.S. government is eager to enhance Nigeria’s capacity as a leading player in the creative economy and encourage global partnerships. This partnership will create a stream of high-quality, commercially viable content that can compete on the world stage.”

a4462.speaker: Inya Lawal, CEO of Ascend Studios
a4462.name: Inya Lawal
a4462.title: CEO of Ascend Studios
a4462.speech: “We are honored to be selected as the recipient of USAID funding” ; “This collaboration represents a milestone for the Nigerian creative sector and opens opportunities for us to elevate African stories on a global platform. Through this initiative, we are building the infrastructure needed to develop world-class creative talent capable of transforming the industry”

a4503.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a4503.name: William Ruto
a4503.title: President of Kenya
a4503.speech: Announced that he will not sign the Finance Bill 2024, acknowledging that the voices of the people have been heard: said after listening "keenly to the people of Kenya who have said loudly that they want nothing to do with this Finance Bill 2024, I concede and therefore I will not sign the 2024 Finance Bill and it shall subsequently be withdrawn".

a4503.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a4503.name: William Ruto
a4503.title: President of Kenya
a4503.speech: In an address, highlighted his administration's unwavering dedication to reducing the prices of essential goods like 'unga', successfully bringing it down from Sh240 to Sh100, and emphasized their achievements in decreasing fertiliser costs from Sh7,500 to Sh2,500 and strengthening the Kenyan Shilling against the US dollar.

a4503.speaker: Amnesty International and other organisations
a4503.name: Amnesty International and other organisations
a4503.speech: Have alleged that 12 prominent people involved in the protest movement had been abducted in the five days leading up to Tuesday's unrest.

a4503.speaker: KTN News anchor
a4503.name: KTN News anchor
a4503.speech: "In the wake of a detailed coverage of the ongoing protest against the Finance Bill 2024 that has been organised by Gen Z protesters, we would like to inform our viewers that we have received threats from the authorities of intention to shut us down. We would like to inform the public of our commitment to defend public interests and we shall not be cowed by any threats."

a4503.speaker: SaharaReporters (report citing KTN News)
a4503.name: SaharaReporters (report citing KTN News)
a4503.speech: On Tuesday, SaharaReporters reported that KTN News had announced that the Kenyan government threatened to shut down the station.

a4629.speaker: Philip Besiimire, Managing Director of Vodacom Tanzania
a4629.name: Philip Besiimire
a4629.title: Managing Director of Vodacom Tanzania
a4629.speech: According to Besiimire, Vodacom has invested over 4.5tri/- in infrastructure and services, including 3.0tri/- in the past decade to expand network coverage to over 95 per cent of the Tanzanian population: “These investments have enabled the deployment of modern technologies such as 4G and 5G, expanding broadband access to more than 70 per cent of the country and modernising Information and Technology (IT) systems, including our M-Pesa platform. As a result, Vodacom has introduced advanced financial products like Songesha, M-Kob0a and merchant payments on M-Pesa, alongside innovative connectivity services such as Nipige Tafu, Buy for a Friend and Share the Bundle.”

a4629.speaker: Philip Besiimire, Managing Director of Vodacom Tanzania
a4629.name: Philip Besiimire
a4629.title: Managing Director of Vodacom Tanzania
a4629.speech: Reflecting on the company's growth, emphasised Vodacom's unwavering commitment to delivering an exceptional customer experience, underpinned by service excellence and robust data privacy.

a4629.speaker: Zuweina Farah, head of the Vodacom Tanzania Foundation
a4629.name: Zuweina Farah
a4629.title: head of the Vodacom Tanzania Foundation
a4629.speech: “Since inception, Vodacom and its partners, including the Vodafone Foundation, have invested billions of shillings in impactful projects that have improved the lives of over 10 million Tanzanians,” noted Ms Farah.

a4809.speaker: Centre Afrika Obota (press release, signed by Urbain Amegbedji, National Secretary)
a4809.name: Centre Afrika Obota (press release
a4809.title: signed by Urbain Amegbedji, National Secretary)
a4809.speech: States that, with the financial support of the American government through USAID, it observed the 13 March 2011 first-round presidential ballot by deploying 300 observers across the country’s 77 communes covering more than 5,000 polling stations, and makes public the following findings: the voting operations took place in peace and serenity, proof of the maturity of the Beninese people despite a conflict-ridden pre-electoral period; the CENA, despite the short deadline, was able to rise to the challenge of an acceptable organisation, without major incidents but not without failings; the Beninese people took part massively in the ballot; and numerous international and national observers, including those of the Constitutional Court, took part in observing the electoral operations.

a4809.speaker: Centre Afrika Obota (press release, signed by Urbain Amegbedji, National Secretary)
a4809.name: Centre Afrika Obota (press release
a4809.title: signed by Urbain Amegbedji, National Secretary)
a4809.speech: Its observers noted shortcomings relating to the organisation and practices contrary to the laws and regulations, which deserve to be made public and brought to the attention of the institutions responsible for settling electoral disputes: the lack of command of the electorate convened, owing to the absence of an electoral roll known to all actors and made public in accordance with the law; the non-publication of the number of polling stations and their actual locations; the unavailability or non-functioning of the special polling stations announced for the last registered voters without voter cards; the authorisation of voting by derogation for persons holding a voter card but who could not find their polling stations; the total absence of an electoral roll in certain localities such as Linsinli in the district of Dan, commune of Djidja; an inflation of votes by derogation in violation of the law, causing an abnormal overrun of the number of voters in several polling stations; the last-minute change of polling station locations, disorienting many voters; delays in the start of voting operations reaching five hours in localities such as Tchaourou; the unavailability of electoral material or its running out mid-ballot; the low level of training of electoral agents and candidates’ representatives; the failure to systematically post results at polling stations as prescribed by law; the transport of results and electoral material by the vehicles of politicians; and the failure to seal envelopes, notably those of the Constitutional Court, before their transport to the CEA offices.

a4809.speaker: Centre Afrika Obota (press release, signed by Urbain Amegbedji, National Secretary)
a4809.name: Centre Afrika Obota (press release
a4809.title: signed by Urbain Amegbedji, National Secretary)
a4809.speech: Notes that the presidential ballot of 13 March 2011 took place under acceptable conditions of freedom, peace and transparency, and invites political actors to have recourse to the bodies for settling electoral disputes for their various appeals. It calls on the clear-sightedness of the Constitutional Court to rule with fairness and justice on the cases of irregularity noted, and finally invites all the Beninese people to patience and calm while awaiting the court’s verdict.

a4842.speaker: Gladys Thawani Kawiya, senior official from the Catholic Agency for Relief and Development (CARD)
a4842.name: Gladys Thawani Kawiya
a4842.title: senior official from the Catholic Agency for Relief and Development (CARD)
a4842.speech: Disclosed that the assistance is being delivered under the Drought Response Project, a program funded with 170,000 Euros.

a4842.speaker: Sonia Paulino, 31-year-old recipient of the aid
a4842.name: Sonia Paulino
a4842.title: 31-year-old recipient of the aid
a4842.speech: Expressed profound gratitude to the organizations involved: "This support will significantly reduce the hardships we are facing," she said, acknowledging the impact of the aid in improving their living conditions.

a5035.speaker: Janet Yellen, US Treasury Secretary
a5035.name: Janet Yellen
a5035.title: US Treasury Secretary
a5035.speech: Said that "a thriving Africa is in the interest of the US," meaning "a larger market for our goods and services," "more investment opportunities for our businesses" and that "more Americans can benefit from the dynamism and creativity of people in Africa" ; said "a pillar of the US strategy towards Africa is boosting mutually beneficial trade and investment," noting the US is South Africa's third-largest trading partner and South Africa is the US's largest trading partner in Africa, and that "in the coming years, we intend to build on that strong foundation to promote even deeper economic integration here, as well as with other African countries."

a5035.speaker: Janet Yellen, US Treasury Secretary
a5035.name: Janet Yellen
a5035.title: US Treasury Secretary
a5035.speech: Noted that Africa is undergoing a significant demographic boom, with Africans projected to make up a quarter of the world's population by 2050, presenting "an extraordinary economic opportunity"; said that under AGOA the US has for over two decades given eligible sub-Saharan African countries duty-free access, that South Africa was the biggest beneficiary last year, and that since 2021 the US has helped close more than 800 trade and investment deals in Africa totalling $18 billion.

a5035.speaker: Janet Yellen, US Treasury Secretary
a5035.name: Janet Yellen
a5035.title: US Treasury Secretary
a5035.speech: Said "the US strongly supports the African Continental Free Trade Area" because trade between African countries has the potential to boost good jobs and economic opportunity.

a5035.speaker: Janet Yellen, US Treasury Secretary
a5035.name: Janet Yellen
a5035.title: US Treasury Secretary
a5035.speech: Said that through the Millennium Challenge Corporation and the Development Finance Corporation the US has more than $10 billion of active commitments and programmes in Africa, and that "I have personally convened the multilateral development banks to urge them to step up policy and technical assistance - as well as financing - in infrastructure."

a5035.speaker: Janet Yellen, US Treasury Secretary
a5035.name: Janet Yellen
a5035.title: US Treasury Secretary
a5035.speech: "Let me be clear: we do not take our investments lightly. Our projects and partnerships are motivated by our mutually beneficial, long-term partnership. That's why we have rigorous accountability, transparency and technical standards. And that's why we assist countries with policy reform and capacity building." ; said people in Africa "are interested in economic arrangements that are fair and open" and that the US shares "a recognition of the importance of strong, open, and accountable institutions."

a5035.speaker: Janet Yellen, US Treasury Secretary
a5035.name: Janet Yellen
a5035.title: US Treasury Secretary
a5035.speech: Said US-Africa integration furthers US security interests, that "Covid-19 brought the world's economic activity to a standstill" and "Russia's brutal war against Ukraine has raised energy prices and exacerbated food insecurity," and that the US is "addressing the over-concentration of the production of critical goods in certain markets - particularly those that may not share our economic values" by deepening integration with trusted trading partners such as South Africa ; "Success in Africa means success for all of us. A thriving Africa helps support a thriving America. The US is committed to working with you to deepen our ties: not for show, not for the short term - but for the long haul."

a5035.speaker: G7
a5035.name: G7
a5035.speech: Has announced a Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment, an initiative aiming to mobilise $600 billion into a variety of quality infrastructure projects by 2027 - including in Africa.

a5035.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a5035.name: Joe Biden
a5035.title: US President
a5035.speech: Announced an initiative on digital transformation last month, under which the US intends to invest over $350 million and facilitate over $450 million in financing for the continent, with funds going towards expanding internet access and enabling a vibrant digital ecosystem through digital skills and literacy.

a5442.speaker: Inocencio Impissa, Mozambican government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration
a5442.name: Inocencio Impissa
a5442.title: Mozambican government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration
a5442.speech: Told reporters on Friday that the Mozambican government is already paying the New Year bonus (the “13th month”) to state employees, and hopes to complete the payment by Tuesday ; said the 13th month would be paid, but only in February, with only 50 per cent of the bonus paid for most of the public service and 100 per cent for state pensioners ; said that so far about 50 per cent of all workers of the public administration have received their 13th month, and that he believed the rest will be paid by next Tuesday, assuming that the state institutions they work for submit the relevant wage sheets on time ; was confident that the missing wage sheets would arrive, and payment would then be made.

a5442.speaker: Inocencio Impissa, Mozambican government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration
a5442.name: Inocencio Impissa
a5442.title: Mozambican government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration
a5442.speech: Asked about the teachers who are refusing to mark the end-of-year examination papers until they are paid for the overtime they have worked, said the government is still in dialogue with the teachers ; stressed that payment of teachers' basic wages is up-to-date, and the only question is when the overtime will be paid ; added that, in the first 100 days of the new government, overtime should be held to a minimum, and that as from now, overtime worked by teachers must be paid the following month, to avoid the accumulation of debts to the teachers.

a5442.speaker: Inocencio Impissa, Mozambican government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration
a5442.name: Inocencio Impissa
a5442.title: Mozambican government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration
a5442.speech: Said the government is speaking with representatives of the United States government in an attempt to reverse the decision to suspend foreign aid ; said the suspension would have a strong impact on Mozambique, even though life-saving aid in the health sector is supposed to be exempt ; called for those affected by the cuts to stay calm, and assured them that the government is attempting to reverse or mitigate the effects and was also seeking to mobilise alternative sources of funding ; added that the government will also “redefine priorities and make the best use of existing resources” to minimise the impact of the cuts on essential services ; “The sudden withdrawal of this support to some extent compromises efficiency in the implementation of these programmes” ; noted that Mozambique has a ratio of 18.5 health professionals per each 10,000 inhabitants against the World Health Organisation target of 45: “We are a very long way from this target, and this suspension decreed by the United States will impose an enormous challenge for us meeting the target”.

a5442.speaker: Inocencio Impissa, Mozambican government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration
a5442.name: Inocencio Impissa
a5442.title: Mozambican government spokesperson and Minister of State Administration
a5442.speech: Promised that from now on the government will give regular, weekly press briefings, meeting with journalists every Friday.

a5442.speaker: Adriano Maleiane, then Prime Minister of Mozambique
a5442.name: Adriano Maleiane
a5442.title: then Prime Minister of Mozambique
a5442.speech: Shortly before Christmas, announced that the government does not have enough money to pay the bonus. He claimed that the state budget only contained enough money to pay the December wage bill, and to solve “some specific questions, particularly with regard to education” (a reference to the overtime payments that teachers had been demanding for months).

a5442.speaker: Trade unions representing some workers in the Mozambican public service
a5442.name: Trade unions representing some workers in the Mozambican public service
a5442.speech: Immediately threatened to go on strike.

a5442.speaker: Trump administration
a5442.name: Trump administration
a5442.speech: Announced that the suspension of foreign aid is initially only for 90 days.

a5484.speaker: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo, Minister of State, Government Spokesperson of Burkina Faso
a5484.name: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo
a5484.title: Minister of State, Government Spokesperson of Burkina Faso
a5484.speech: Said the Council of Ministers examined files and adopted several reports important for the proper running of the Nation ; on the project for the acquisition of 500 buses to improve SOTRACO's capacity to respond to mobility needs in urban centres, particularly for pupils and students: "This project will cost a total of 44,865,000,000 CFA francs excluding taxes."

a5484.speaker: Commander Ismael Sombie, Minister of Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Resources of Burkina Faso
a5484.name: Commander Ismael Sombie
a5484.title: Minister of Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Resources of Burkina Faso
a5484.speech: Said that during the present wet agricultural season, production is estimated at about 6,077,000 tonnes of cereals against 5,147,000 tonnes produced during the 2023 season: "This is truly significant and represents an increase of nearly 18.07% compared with the previous season and of 21.4% compared with the average of the seasons of the last five years."

a5484.speaker: Commander Ismael Sombie, Minister of Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Resources of Burkina Faso
a5484.name: Commander Ismael Sombie
a5484.title: Minister of Agriculture, Animal and Fishery Resources of Burkina Faso
a5484.speech: Indicated that, to guarantee better accessibility for all consumers, measures are being taken by the government to ban the export of cereals on the one hand, and on the other hand, to strengthen the capacities of SONAGESS as well as price controls.

a5484.speaker: Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, Minister of Economy and Finance of Burkina Faso
a5484.name: Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo
a5484.title: Minister of Economy and Finance of Burkina Faso
a5484.speech: Said the objective of the preliminary draft law regulating tax advisory services in Burkina Faso is to regulate the tax advisory profession.

a5484.speaker: Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, Minister of Economy and Finance of Burkina Faso
a5484.name: Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo
a5484.title: Minister of Economy and Finance of Burkina Faso
a5484.speech: Said the draft decree on the procedures for the award, execution and settlement of public contracts contains several innovations essentially intended to allow young companies to have many more possibilities in terms of public contracts.

a5484.speaker: Yacouba Zabre Gouba, Minister of Energy, Mines and Quarries of Burkina Faso
a5484.name: Yacouba Zabre Gouba
a5484.title: Minister of Energy, Mines and Quarries of Burkina Faso
a5484.speech: Said that through the decree on the establishment, creation, organisation and functioning of a national technical commission on mines, the aim is to make the National Mines Commission much more operational.

a5701.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa (official statement published on the South African presidency website)
a5701.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a5701.title: President of South Africa (official statement published on the South African presidency website)
a5701.speech: "South Africa is a constitutional democracy deeply rooted in the rule of law, justice and equality" ; responding to criticism of the new expropriation law, he made clear that it is in no way a policy of confiscation: "The South African government has not confiscated any land. The recently adopted Expropriation Act is not an instrument of confiscation, but a legal procedure prescribed by the Constitution that ensures public access to land in an equitable and just manner" ; "South Africa, like the United States of America and other countries, has always had expropriation laws that balance the need for public use of land and the protection of rights."

a5701.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa (official statement)
a5701.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a5701.title: President of South Africa (official statement)
a5701.speech: Underlining the importance of US-South African relations, showed himself open to dialogue: "We look forward to engaging with the Trump administration on our land reform policy [...] We are confident that from these engagements we will share a better common understanding of these issues" ; recalled that "the United States remains a key strategic and trade partner for South Africa", while specifying that "apart from PEPFAR Aid, which represents 17% of the South African HIV/AIDS programme, there is no other significant funding provided by the United States in South Africa."

a5735.speaker: Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (Macra)
a5735.name: Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (Macra)
a5735.speech: Says the equipment procured to monitor and evaluate the state of misinformation and disinformation in Malawi is important to check the trend.

a5735.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5735.name: Donald Trump
a5735.title: US President
a5735.speech: Emphasising “America First”, ordered a nine-month stop order on US aid global projects.

a5780.speaker: Dr. Kayad Moussa Ahmed, Director General of the Djiboutian Office for the Development of Geothermal Energy (ODDEG)
a5780.name: Dr. Kayad Moussa Ahmed
a5780.title: Director General of the Djiboutian Office for the Development of Geothermal Energy (ODDEG)
a5780.speech: Declared: “The introduction of this equipment and the associated training constitutes a major advance for ODDEG and the geothermal sector in Djibouti. It strengthens our capacity to explore and sustainably develop the geothermal resources of our country.”

a5780.speaker: Dr. Kayad Moussa Ahmed, Director General of ODDEG
a5780.name: Dr. Kayad Moussa Ahmed
a5780.title: Director General of ODDEG
a5780.speech: Had a discussion with the United States Ambassador on the acquisition of this equipment, which represents a substantial gain in terms of reduced costs and time: traditionally ODDEG had to send its samples abroad for analysis, which entailed additional costs and considerable delays, whereas thanks to the X-ray fluorescence analyser and the other equipment ODDEG will now be able to carry out its own analyses directly on site, reducing dependence on external providers.

a5780.speaker: Engineers of ODDEG
a5780.name: Engineers of ODDEG
a5780.speech: During the visit, presented the equipment of ODDEG’s various laboratories and more particularly the geoscience equipment — the XRF, seismic and separator equipment supplied by USAID.

a5780.speaker: Cynthia Kiercht, United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a5780.name: Cynthia Kiercht
a5780.title: United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a5780.speech: Visited ODDEG’s geoscience laboratories, highlighting the professionalism of the engineers and the importance of international cooperation for Djibouti.

a5783.speaker: Amanda Roberson, Portuguese-language spokesperson for the United States Department of State
a5783.name: Amanda Roberson
a5783.title: Portuguese-language spokesperson for the United States Department of State
a5783.speech: Said in conversation with Expresso das Ilhas that “Putting the United States first does not mean that we are going to work alone”: the well-known “America First” motto that has guided US policy in the Trump administrations seems more current than ever, but that does not mean the country will work in isolation from the rest of the world; the relationship with other nations will continue to be fostered, and the expectation is that they too will gain from the approach and likewise become more prosperous and secure. The interview, part of a State Department initiative to present monthly-defined topics on Washington’s new global foreign policy to the PALOP (African Countries with Portuguese as an Official Language), covered themes from immigration to the suspension of USAID, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and South Africa.

a5952.speaker: The World Bank
a5952.name: The World Bank
a5952.speech: Ranked Burkina Faso as the 13th poorest country in the world in 2002.

a5952.speaker: UNDP 2005 Human Development Index
a5952.name: UNDP 2005 Human Development Index
a5952.speech: Ranked Burkina Faso at 175 out of 177 countries.

a5952.speaker: UK Foreign and Commonwealth Office, ‘Human Rights Report’
a5952.name: UK Foreign and Commonwealth Office
a5952.title: ‘Human Rights Report’
a5952.speech: Lists Somalia as a country of concern, reflecting its very poor human rights record.

a5952.speaker: UNAIDS/WHO Working Group, 2008 Report on the Global AIDS Epidemic
a5952.name: UNAIDS/WHO Working Group
a5952.title: 2008 Report on the Global AIDS Epidemic
a5952.speech: Estimated that around 73,000 adults aged 15 or over in Congo were living with HIV, a prevalence rate of around 3.5% of the adult population.

a6069.speaker: Write-up on HOO-IMM PLUS by HOOTONE REMEDIES
a6069.name: Write-up on HOO-IMM PLUS by HOOTONE REMEDIES
a6069.speech: According to a write-up, this drug is absolutely new, novel, pioneering and revolutionary concept from HOOTONE REMEDIES to medical science. “It is a very safe, efficacious Indian medicine for the relief of AIDS according to the degree and stage of affliction. This our herbal preparation has not only recorded the highest inhibition rate, i.e. 98 percent against the causative agent HIV in invitro anti-retroviral activity drug sensitivity.” The write-up says the drug is a polyherbal formula of 33 different plant species and has active compounds inhibiting various steps in the HIV life circle.

a6145.speaker: UNICEF
a6145.name: UNICEF
a6145.speech: According to UNICEF, the number of displaced children has doubled in just one year in Haiti, which demonstrates "the rapid deterioration of the situation and its profound impact on the country's most vulnerable boys, girls and families."

a6145.speaker: Bruno Maes, UNICEF Representative in Haiti
a6145.name: Bruno Maes
a6145.title: UNICEF Representative in Haiti
a6145.speech: Lamented how these "relentless waves of brutal violence" leave behind "new horrors" and "an ever-present shadow of fear" among the population ; "It is a humanitarian catastrophe unfolding before our eyes," Maes warned in a statement ; "We cannot stand idly by while the future of Haiti's children is eroded by endless suffering. Every moment of inaction aggravates the crisis that is consuming their lives," stressed Maes, who asked the international community for help with the aim of achieving "hope and change" for young people.

a6145.speaker: UNICEF
a6145.name: UNICEF
a6145.speech: Denounced the blocking of basic services, including health and education, and the recurring violations of children's rights, who are threatened in particular with forced recruitment.

a6145.speaker: UN
a6145.name: UN
a6145.speech: The UN fears that the number of children needing humanitarian assistance will increase if conditions on the ground get worse.

a6145.speaker: UNICEF
a6145.name: UNICEF
a6145.speech: Has requested 221.7 million dollars [204.6 million euros] to carry out its programmes in 2024.

a6203.speaker: Berkha Africa (statement)
a6203.name: Berkha Africa (statement)
a6203.speech: Has commended Scofray Nana Yaw Yeboah for becoming Ghana’s first Master Certified Coach (MCC) from the International Coaching Federation (ICF); the statement explained that his elevation to MCC status represents a transformational boost for Ghana’s leadership development space, especially at a time when the corporate sector is seeking expertise for deeper leadership capacity, ethical business culture and productivity through people-centred strategy. “With 64 MCC holders in Africa, this credential represents the gold standard in professional coaching, awarded only to those who demonstrate exceptional mastery of the ICF Core Competencies, deep commitment to ethical practice and extensive coaching experience,” the statement said.

a6203.speaker: Rev. James A. Godly, Executive Lead for Global Partnerships for Berkha Africa (signed statement)
a6203.name: Rev. James A. Godly
a6203.title: Executive Lead for Global Partnerships for Berkha Africa (signed statement)
a6203.speech: Explained that the MCC credential, which required more than 2,500 hours of client coaching experience and rigorous evaluation, equipped coaches to deliver world-class coaching engagements tailored to both executive and organisational development needs. “The distinct approach of our Master Coach Scofray, who is also CEO of Zoweh Global Consult and President of International Coaching Federation, Ghana Chapter, emphasises clarity, purpose-driven leadership, emotional intelligence and sustainable transformation; values that are at the heart of Berkha Africa’s mission.” ; “In addition to this distinction, Scofray, who has achieved more than 3,500 coaching hours, is also recognised as the world’s first Black Professional Certified mBIT Trainer in Africa and the first past learner of the Institute of Commercial Management (UK) to attain Fellow status globally, further underlining his unmatched credentials in the fields of coaching, leadership and human transformation.” ; “Berkha Africa considers this achievement a strategic advantage to its clients and partners across Africa, especially at a time when businesses are grappling with complex challenges in sustainable leadership, culture, talent retention, ethical and progressive institutional performance,” it said, adding that “Master Coach Scofray’s global-level certification is expected to enrich Berkha’s coaching suite, which includes leadership/executive coaching, development coaching, performance and team coaching.”

a6221.speaker: Supporters of the bill (as reported by the international press)
a6221.name: Supporters of the bill (as reported by the international press)
a6221.speech: Argue that the bill will allow members of Congress to exercise their functions independently, without fear of political persecution or judicial summonses.

a6244.speaker: Stefan Wolff, Professor of International Security, University of Birmingham, and Tatyana Malyarenko, Professor of International Relations, National University Odesa Law Academy
a6244.name: Stefan Wolff
a6244.title: Professor of International Security, University of Birmingham, and Tatyana Malyarenko, Professor of International Relations, National University Odesa Law Academy
a6244.speech: Write that, considering that no country has recognised the annexation by Russia of the Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhya and Kherson regions, Moscow is clearly on its own when it comes to its illegal land grab in Ukraine; argue that Biden's visit underscores that the west has every confidence that the Russian president will not win this war and is finally coming round to the idea of providing Ukraine with what it needs to defeat Russia; and conclude that western leaders should not become comfortable with a “forever war” and must step up their support and enable Ukraine to defeat this Russian aggression and restore its full sovereignty and territorial integrity.

a6244.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a6244.name: Vladimir Putin
a6244.title: Russian President
a6244.speech: Still insists on calling the invasion a “special military operation”, which he expected to be completed swiftly and successfully; three days before the invasion he had recognised the so-called Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics.

a6244.speaker: Ukraine Support Tracker, Kiel Institute for the World Economy
a6244.name: Ukraine Support Tracker
a6244.title: Kiel Institute for the World Economy
a6244.speech: More than €40 billion (£33.25 billion) worth of military assistance was offered to Ukraine by mid-November 2022, more than half of it provided by the US, with the UK, EU institutions and Germany the next-largest contributors.

a6244.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission
a6244.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a6244.title: President of the European Commission
a6244.speech: Reiterated in her speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos on January 13 that the west will back Ukraine against Russia “for as long as it takes”.

a6244.speaker: China (Beijing)
a6244.name: China (Beijing)
a6244.speech: Has repeatedly indicated sympathy for Russia's decision to invade, but has remained steadfast in supporting Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity to date; has also warned Russia against meddling in others of its neighbours.

a6491.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a6491.name: Government of Mozambique
a6491.speech: Said on Friday that the suspension of US international aid has compromised health programmes in Mozambique, especially HIV/AIDS, and that it is in ongoing “dialogue” with the US embassy to “mitigate the impacts”.

a6491.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, spokesman for the Mozambican government and minister of state administration and civil service
a6491.name: Inocêncio Impissa
a6491.title: spokesman for the Mozambican government and minister of state administration and civil service
a6491.speech: “The abrupt withdrawal of this support compromises, as you can imagine in some way, the efficiency of the implementation of these programmes (…) The support of the American government finances a considerable part of the provision of health professionals and above all in the area of HIV/AIDS care” ; Recognising the “seriousness of the measures” announced by US president Donald Trump, he nevertheless guaranteed the continuity of essential health services, urging the public not to panic ; said the suspension of funding also has implications for the purchase and distribution of medicines, and stressed the importance of support to maintain strategic and priority health programmes such as the fight against HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis ; “Both the central warehouse and the regional warehouses are going to experience some overload of medicines over the next few days because the logistics of transporting them to the points where they need to be distributed [has] been disrupted” ; “We are a long way off and this suspension of support is naturally a huge challenge if we are to reach this target” ; “The government has started a dialogue with the United States to reverse or mitigate the scenario of the suspension of funding, but also to mobilise alternative sources of funding” ; said it would be necessary to define priorities and optimise the country’s existing resources in order to minimise the impact on essential services ; “We need to prioritise what should effectively not be missed during the period in which this measure is in place, but also explore emergency funding mechanisms to guarantee the continuity of critical services until a durable and sustainable solution is in fact found.”

a6491.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6491.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6491.speech: Has established a ratio of 45 health professionals per 10,000 inhabitants, but Mozambique has just over 18 professionals per 10,000 inhabitants (cited by the minister).

a6491.speaker: Marco Rubio, US secretary of state and new acting director of USAID
a6491.name: Marco Rubio
a6491.title: US secretary of state and new acting director of USAID
a6491.speech: Accused USAID of being “completely lacking in response capacity”, criticising the “insubordination” in that body.

a6491.speaker: Donald Trump, US president; Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE); and some Republican congressmen
a6491.name: Donald Trump
a6491.title: US president; Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE); and some Republican congressmen
a6491.speech: Have criticised USAID – which oversees humanitarian, development and security programmes in around 120 countries – in increasingly harsh terms, accusing it of promoting progressive causes.

a6552.speaker: Fahad Bin Abdulrahman H. Aldosari, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Burkina Faso
a6552.name: Fahad Bin Abdulrahman H. Aldosari
a6552.title: Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Burkina Faso
a6552.speech: Explained that the project, worth 1.8 million dollars, is a gift from Saudi Arabia to the Burkinabe State. "This project coincides with the celebration of the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Burkina Faso and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and of the 95th anniversary of the unification of Saudi Arabia, celebrated every 23 September," he specified ; Stressed that, within the framework of bilateral cooperation, his country has carried out several projects in Burkina Faso: "Saudi Arabia is carrying out projects worth 1,000 billion CFA francs across more than 80 projects for the Burkinabe people."

a6552.speaker: Al Moubareck Ag Mohamed, president of the NGO Association for Human Benevolence (ABH)
a6552.name: Al Moubareck Ag Mohamed
a6552.title: president of the NGO Association for Human Benevolence (ABH)
a6552.speech: Indicated that the beneficiaries of the project were selected in perfect collaboration between the NGO and the services of the ministry in charge of humanitarian action in each targeted locality.

a6552.speaker: Adama Dofini, director of programmes of the Burkina Faso Red Cross
a6552.name: Adama Dofini
a6552.title: director of programmes of the Burkina Faso Red Cross
a6552.speech: Thanked the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for this gesture on behalf of the community of internally displaced persons.

a6552.speaker: Imam Aboubacar Yugo, president of the presidium of the Federation of Islamic Associations of Burkina Faso
a6552.name: Imam Aboubacar Yugo
a6552.title: president of the presidium of the Federation of Islamic Associations of Burkina Faso
